etymology_story.zh: 英语在19世纪从美洲西班牙语借入 cholo，其更早来源存在争议；早期常涉及混合血统或原住民身份，后来在美国又发展出贬称及街头亚文化身份称呼等用法。部分群体将其重新用作自称，因此语气必须结合地域、说话者与语境判断。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/cholo)；[秘鲁语言科学院词源研究](https://revistas.apl.org.pe/index.php/boletinapl/article/view/388)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed cholo from American Spanish in the nineteenth century; its earlier origin is disputed, and meanings concerning mixed or Indigenous ancestry later developed alongside disparaging and street-subculture uses in the United States. Some communities have reclaimed it as a self-description, so its tone depends on region, speaker, and context. [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/cholo); [Peruvian Academy etymological study](https://revistas.apl.org.pe/index.php/boletinapl/article/view/388)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 cholo 作为整体借词处理，不宜把 chol- 当作可自由构词的英语词根。相关形式：cholos（复数）、chola（女性对应称呼）、cholas（其复数）、cholo-style（乔洛风格的）；西班牙语中的 -o/-a 性别对应不构成英语中普遍能产的规则。cholo culture 等通常分析为名词作定语，而非另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cholo is a borrowed base; chol- should not be treated as a freely productive English root. Related forms include cholos, the female counterpart chola and its plural cholas, and cholo-style. The Spanish -o/-a gender correspondence is not a generally productive English rule. Uses such as cholo culture are normally analyzed as noun modification rather than a separate common adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: mestizo（欧洲人与美洲原住民混合血统者）主要描述祖源，不自动带有街头亚文化含义；Chicano（奇卡诺人）主要是墨西哥裔美国人的文化或政治身份称呼；gang member（帮派成员）只描述帮派身份，不能作为所有 cholos 的同义称呼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Mestizo primarily describes mixed European and Indigenous American ancestry without automatically implying street culture; Chicano primarily denotes a Mexican American cultural or political identity; gang member describes gang affiliation and is not a synonym for every person called a cholo.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词记作“地域身份标签”：祖源、贬称、街头认同三种用法，先看语境。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember a regional identity label with three contextual readings: ancestry, insult, or street-cultural identity.

meaning: 语境化；放在相关背景中理解

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 通常不可数；英式也写 contextualisation。
family: contextualize 使语境化；contextual 语境的；contextualisation 英式拼写

morphology.text: contextualize（置于语境中）+ -ation（行为、过程）→ contextualization（语境化），词尾 e 脱落。

etymology.text: 现代英语在 contextualize 后加名词后缀 -ation 形成；其词基 context 更早来自拉丁语 contextus，含“编织在一起”的意思。把一句话与周围背景编在一起理解。

usage_note: 常见于语言、历史和研究说明，指补上背景以理解材料；不是把材料脱离背景摘出来。

senses.meaning_zh: 语境化；结合有关背景、情境或上下文进行理解或呈现
senses.meaning_en: The process of understanding or presenting something in relation to its relevant background or circumstances.
senses.english_definition: Contextualization is the process of placing something in its surrounding circumstances so that its meaning or importance becomes clearer.
senses.collocation_en: historical contextualization; cultural contextualization
senses.collocation_zh: 置于历史背景中理解；置于文化背景中理解
senses.sentence_en: Historical contextualization helps readers understand why the novel was controversial.
senses.sentence_zh: 结合历史背景进行解读，有助于读者理解这部小说为何曾引发争议。

etymology_story.zh: 这是由 contextualize（置于语境中）与名词后缀 -ation 构成的现代英语名词；其基础词 context 最终源自拉丁语 contextus，与 contexere（编织在一起）相关。含义由文字之间的联系扩展到事物与历史、文化或情境背景之间的联系。[词源词典](https://www.etymonline.com/word/context)
etymology_story.en: This modern English noun is formed from contextualize and the noun-forming suffix -ation; its base context ultimately comes from Latin contextus, associated with contexere, to weave together. The underlying idea expanded from connections within a text to connections with historical, cultural, or situational circumstances. [Online Etymology Dictionary](https://www.etymonline.com/word/context)

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词链：context（语境；背景）+ -ual → contextual（语境的）+ -ize → contextualize（使语境化）；去掉末尾 e，加 -ation → contextualization。主要词族：context、contexts、contextual、contextually、contextualize、contextualizes、contextualized、contextualizing、contextualization；另有 contextualise、contextualisation 等 -ise/-isation 拼写，以及 decontextualize/decontextualization（使脱离语境／脱离语境的过程）、recontextualize/recontextualization（重新置于语境中／重新语境化）、contextualism/contextualist（语境主义／语境主义者或语境主义的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation chain: context + -ual → contextual; contextual + -ize → contextualize; remove final e and add -ation → contextualization. The main family includes context, contexts, contextual, contextually, contextualize, contextualizes, contextualized, contextualizing, and contextualization. It also includes -ise/-isation spellings such as contextualise and contextualisation; decontextualize/decontextualization, meaning removal from context; recontextualize/recontextualization, meaning placement in a new context; and contextualism/contextualist, referring to context-centered approaches and their advocates.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: framing（框定；设定理解框架）强调选择解读角度；situating（置于背景中）强调确定事物在较大环境中的位置；background explanation（背景说明）强调补充背景信息。contextualization 更明确强调事物与相关环境之间有助于理解的联系。[剑桥词典](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/contextualization)
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Framing emphasizes the interpretive perspective selected; situating emphasizes locating something within a wider setting; background explanation emphasizes supplying supporting information. Contextualization more explicitly connects something with the circumstances needed to understand it. [Cambridge Dictionary](https://dictionary.cambridge.org/dictionary/english/contextualization)

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把事物与背景“编织在一起”：context 是背景，contextualization 是放回背景中理解。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Weave the thing together with its background: context supplies the setting, and contextualization connects it to that setting.

meaning: 民族音乐学；从社会文化背景研究音乐的学科
aliases: 从社会文化背景研究音乐的学科

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 学科名，通常不可数。
family: ethnomusicologist 民族音乐学家；ethnomusicologists 复数

morphology.text: ethno-（民族、文化群体）+ musicology（音乐学）→ ethnomusicology（民族音乐学）。

etymology.text: 现代英语由 ethno- 与 musicology 组合，前者来自希腊语 ethnos（民族、群体）。从音乐走向演奏者及其文化生活，就能记住学科关注点。

usage_note: 当代用法重视音乐的社会文化背景，并不限于收集异国曲调；本课采用这一较宽的学科义。

senses.meaning_zh: 民族音乐学；研究音乐及其社会文化背景的学科
senses.meaning_en: The study of music in its social and cultural contexts.
senses.english_definition: Ethnomusicology is the study of how people make, use, and understand music within their cultures and societies.
senses.collocation_en: study ethnomusicology; ethnomusicology research
senses.collocation_zh: 学习民族音乐学；民族音乐学研究
senses.sentence_en: Her research in ethnomusicology explores how wedding songs express a community's values.
senses.sentence_zh: 她的民族音乐学研究探讨婚礼歌曲如何表达一个社群的价值观。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 ethno-（民族、文化群体）与 musicology（音乐学）组合而成，ethno- 最终源于希腊语 ethnos（民族、群体）。这一名称随着研究者对音乐的文化背景和社会生活的关注而广泛使用。
etymology_story.en: The word combines ethno-, meaning a people or cultural group and ultimately derived from Greek ethnos, with musicology. The name gained currency as researchers increasingly emphasized music's cultural settings and its place in social life.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：ethno-（民族、文化群体）+ musicology（音乐学）；后者可分析为 music（音乐）+ -ology（研究、学科）。主要词族：ethnomusicologist（民族音乐学家）、ethnomusicological（民族音乐学的）、ethnomusicologically（从民族音乐学角度）；基础相关词包括 musicology（音乐学）、musicologist（音乐学家）和 musicological（音乐学的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: ethno- (a people or cultural group) + musicology; musicology can itself be analyzed as music + -ology (study or a field of knowledge). Principal family members are ethnomusicologist, ethnomusicological, and ethnomusicologically; related base words include musicology, musicologist, and musicological.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 近义或相关术语：anthropology of music（音乐人类学）突出人类学视角；musicology（音乐学）是范围更广的音乐研究；comparative musicology（比较音乐学）是相关的历史学科名称，强调跨文化比较，不能与现代民族音乐学完全等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: anthropology of music emphasizes an anthropological perspective; musicology is the broader study of music; comparative musicology is a historical disciplinary term emphasizing comparison across cultures and is not fully interchangeable with modern ethnomusicology.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ethno- 是“人群与文化”：研究音乐，也研究音乐背后的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ethno- points to people and culture: study the music together with the people behind it.

meaning: 小知识；简短而常不重要的事实
aliases: 简短而常不重要的事实

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 可数；复数 factoids。
family: factoids 小知识（复数）；fact 事实

morphology.text: fact（事实）+ -oid（像……的）→ factoid；这个词后来也常指简短的小知识。

etymology.text: 由英语 fact 与表示“像……的”希腊语来源后缀 -oid 组成；最初可指被印成文字后让人当真的假事实，后来也用于小知识。记住两个意思都要靠语境分辨。

usage_note: 本课选择“小知识”义。这个词还可指未经证实却被当真的说法，因此看到 factoid 不能自动断定内容真假。

senses.meaning_zh: 小知识；简短而有趣、通常不甚重要的事实
senses.meaning_en: A brief, interesting, usually minor piece of factual information.
senses.english_definition: A factoid is a small piece of information that people find interesting, even though it may not be very important.
senses.collocation_en: an interesting factoid; a fun factoid
senses.collocation_zh: 一条有趣的小知识；一条趣味小知识
senses.sentence_en: The guide shared an interesting factoid about the building's unusual roof.
senses.sentence_zh: 导游分享了一条关于这座建筑独特屋顶的有趣小知识。

senses.meaning_zh: 伪事实；因被刊载或反复传播而被当真的无根据说法
senses.meaning_en: An unsupported or false claim accepted as fact because it appears in print or is repeatedly circulated.
senses.english_definition: A factoid is a claim that people accept as true because it has been published or repeated, although it has not been properly established.
senses.collocation_en: a widely repeated factoid; an unsubstantiated factoid
senses.collocation_zh: 一则被广泛重复的伪事实；一则缺乏证据的所谓事实
senses.sentence_en: The article challenged a widely repeated factoid about how memory works.
senses.sentence_zh: 这篇文章质疑了一则关于记忆运作方式、被广泛传播的伪事实。

etymology_story.zh: 美国作家诺曼·梅勒在1973年的《玛丽莲》中创造了 factoid，以 fact（事实）加上表示“像……的”的 -oid，指因见诸文字而获得事实外观的无根据说法。后来，该词也发展出“简短有趣的小知识”这一常见含义。
etymology_story.en: Norman Mailer coined factoid in his 1973 book Marilyn, adding -oid, meaning resembling, to fact to describe unsupported claims that acquire the appearance of truth through publication. The word later developed the common meaning of a brief, interesting piece of information.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：fact（事实）+ -oid（像……的、具有……外观的）→ factoid；规则复数为 factoids。没有庞大的常用派生词族；factoid-like（像小知识或伪事实的）是可理解的临时复合形式，factual（事实的）和 factually（依据事实地）属于基础词 fact 的相关词族。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: fact + -oid (resembling or having the appearance of) → factoid; the regular plural is factoids. There is no large common derivational family; factoid-like is a transparent occasional compound, while factual and factually belong to the related family of the base word fact.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 小知识义：trivia（琐碎知识）通常作集合性表达，tidbit（趣闻、零星消息）突出短小有趣。伪事实义：myth（流行误解）强调被普遍相信的错误观念；factoid 更突出说法看似事实以及传播赋予它的可信外观。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: For the minor-information sense, trivia usually refers collectively to small facts, while tidbit emphasizes an appealing little piece of information. For the unsupported-claim sense, myth emphasizes a widely held false belief; factoid highlights a claim's factual appearance and the credibility it gains through circulation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: fact + -oid＝“长得像事实”：先记伪事实，再联想后来引申的“小块事实”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fact + -oid means fact-shaped: remember the original questionable claim, then the later little-fact meaning.

meaning: 费米子；自旋为半奇整数的粒子
aliases: 自旋为半奇整数的粒子

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 可数；复数 fermions。
family: fermions 费米子（复数）；fermionic 费米子的

morphology.text: Fermi（费米的姓）+ -on（粒子名称成分）→ fermion（费米子），保留姓氏的主体。

etymology.text: 现代物理英语为纪念物理学家 Enrico Fermi，在 Fermi 后加粒子名成分 -on。把科学家的姓与这类粒子连在一起记。

usage_note: 电子、质子、中子都是费米子的例子；不把所有粒子都叫 fermion。普通粒子名称用小写，科学家姓氏 Fermi 大写。

senses.meaning_zh: 费米子；遵循费米–狄拉克统计、具有半奇整数自旋的粒子
senses.meaning_en: A particle with half-integer spin that obeys Fermi–Dirac statistics.
senses.english_definition: A fermion is a particle, such as an electron, with half-integer spin that obeys rules preventing two identical particles from occupying exactly the same quantum state.
senses.collocation_en: an elementary fermion; a composite fermion
senses.collocation_zh: 基本费米子；复合费米子

etymology_story.zh: fermion 以物理学家恩里科·费米的姓氏 Fermi 为基础，加上粒子名称中常见的 -on 构成。这个名称体现了费米与费米–狄拉克统计的联系，用来指遵循这种统计规律的粒子。
etymology_story.en: Fermion was formed from the surname of physicist Enrico Fermi with -on, a common ending in particle names. The name reflects Fermi's association with Fermi–Dirac statistics and denotes particles that obey those statistics.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：Fermi（费米的姓氏）+ -on（粒子名称后缀）→ fermion，拼合时不重复相邻的 i。主要词族：fermions（复数）、fermionic（费米子的）、antifermion（反费米子）；专业派生形式包括 fermionize／fermionise（使费米子化）和 fermionization／fermionisation（费米子化）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: Fermi + -on, a particle-name suffix, → fermion, with the adjacent i letters merged. Principal family members include fermions, fermionic, and antifermion; specialized derivatives include fermionize/fermionise and fermionization/fermionisation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有同样常用且完全等义的单词；half-integer-spin particle（半奇整数自旋粒子）是标准语境中的描述性对应表达。相关术语 lepton（轻子）指一类基本费米子，baryon（重子）指一类复合费米子，二者都只覆盖费米子的部分范围。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no equally common exact single-word synonym; half-integer-spin particle is a descriptive equivalent in the standard context. The related term lepton names a class of elementary fermions, while baryon names a class of composite fermions; neither covers all fermions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Fermi 的粒子名：半奇整数自旋，相同量子态不能由两个全同费米子共享。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Fermi's particle name: half-integer spin, with no two identical fermions sharing the same quantum state.

meaning: 甘纳许；巧克力奶油混合酱

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 通常不可数；说一种配方可用 a ganache。
family: ganache-filled 以甘纳许为馅的

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；ganache + filled → ganache-filled（甘纳许夹心的），说明甜点里填了这种巧克力混合物。

etymology.text: 英语借自法语 ganache，这个名称在法国糖果制作中使用，后来用于巧克力奶油混合物。记忆重点放在糕点表层或夹心的浓滑巧克力上。

usage_note: 通常由巧克力与奶油混合，用作夹心、淋面或糖衣；不是所有 chocolate sauce 都一定是 ganache。

senses.meaning_zh: 甘纳许；通常由巧克力和奶油制成、用作甜点淋面或夹馅的混合物
senses.meaning_en: A chocolate-and-cream mixture used as a glaze, filling, or coating for desserts.
senses.english_definition: Ganache is a smooth mixture of chocolate and cream that you use to fill or cover cakes, pastries, and chocolates.
senses.collocation_en: chocolate ganache; ganache filling
senses.collocation_zh: 巧克力甘纳许；甘纳许夹馅
senses.sentence_en: Let the ganache cool slightly before spreading it over the cake.
senses.sentence_zh: 让甘纳许稍微冷却后，再将它涂在蛋糕上。

etymology_story.zh: 英语 ganache 借自法语中的同名糕点制作术语。法语 ganache 更早还有“下颌”和“笨人”等含义，但它如何具体成为这种巧克力混合物的名称并不确定，流行的厨房失误故事不宜当作已证实的词源。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed ganache from the French confectionery term. The French word had earlier senses including jaw and fool, but the precise route to the chocolate-mixture meaning is uncertain, so popular kitchen-accident stories should not be treated as established etymology.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常视为不可再分析的法语借词，没有可用于解释本义的英语词根与词缀。通常作不可数名词；表示不同种类或配方时可用复数 ganaches；常见复合形式有 ganache-filled（甘纳许夹心的）和 ganache-covered（裹有甘纳许的），没有广泛通用的派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, ganache is normally treated as an unanalyzed French borrowing, without English roots or affixes that explain its meaning. It is usually uncountable, though ganaches can refer to different varieties or recipes; compounds include ganache-filled and ganache-covered, and there is no widely established derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关表达：chocolate glaze（巧克力淋面）强调覆盖用途和流动性，未必含奶油；chocolate frosting（巧克力糖霜）通常是可涂抹的蛋糕表层，配方可能含黄油和糖；chocolate filling（巧克力夹馅）强调用途，范围比 ganache 更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related expressions: chocolate glaze emphasizes a flowing coating and need not contain cream; chocolate frosting is generally a spreadable cake topping that may contain butter and sugar; chocolate filling describes a use and includes mixtures other than ganache.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 整词连画面：巧克力遇上热奶油，变成浓滑的夹心或淋面。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the whole word through a picture: chocolate meets hot cream and becomes a smooth filling or coating.

meaning: 晶洞；内壁长有晶体的空心石体

forms: 可数；复数 geodes。
family: geodes 晶洞（复数）

morphology.text: 整词作为独立词素记忆；geode + -like → geode-like（像晶洞的），用派生形容词描述外壳与晶体内壁的相似外观。

etymology.text: 英语来自拉丁语 geodes，更早是希腊语 geōdēs（像土的），词基 gē 表示“地、土”。外表像普通石块，打开却有晶体，很适合形成画面。

usage_note: 通常指里面有空腔、腔壁附着晶体的石块，也可指其中的空腔；本课取整个石体。

senses.meaning_zh: 晶洞；内部有晶体衬里的空腔、外部通常呈圆形的岩石体
senses.meaning_en: A usually rounded rock containing a cavity lined with crystals.
senses.english_definition: A geode is a rock with a hollow space inside it where crystals have grown along the inner walls.
senses.collocation_en: a quartz geode; an amethyst geode
senses.collocation_zh: 石英晶洞；紫水晶晶洞
senses.sentence_en: When we opened the geode, we found tiny quartz crystals lining the cavity.
senses.sentence_zh: 我们打开这块晶洞石后，发现空腔内壁布满了细小的石英晶体。

etymology_story.zh: geode 经拉丁语 geodes 追溯到希腊语 geōdēs，意为“土质的、像土的”，其中 gē 意为“地、土”。这个较早的矿物名称后来用于指内部带有晶体空腔的石体。
etymology_story.en: Geode comes through Latin geodes from Greek geōdēs, meaning earthy or earthlike, based on gē, meaning earth. The older mineral name came to designate a rock containing a crystal-lined cavity.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 geode 通常作为完整词基处理，不能机械拆成具有现代构词意义的 geo- + -de；历史上可识别出表示“地、土”的希腊语词基。复数为 geodes；相关形式有较少见的形容词 geodic（晶洞的）以及透明复合形式 geode-like（像晶洞的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, geode normally functions as a complete base and should not be mechanically divided into geo- + -de as productive English elements; historically, it contains the Greek base meaning earth. The plural is geodes; related forms include the uncommon adjective geodic and the transparent compound geode-like.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 相关术语：crystal-lined cavity（晶体衬里的空腔）是描述性近义表达，但可能只指内部空腔；vug（晶簇空洞）指岩石中的空洞，常带晶体，却未必具有晶洞石的独立圆形外壳；druse（晶簇）主要指覆盖表面的密集小晶体，强调晶体层。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Related terms: crystal-lined cavity is a descriptive near-equivalent but may refer only to the internal space; vug is a cavity in rock, often containing crystals, without necessarily having a geode's separate rounded shell; druse chiefly denotes a coating or cluster of small crystals and emphasizes the crystal layer.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: geo 联想到土地：外面一块土石，里面一座水晶小洞。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect geo with earth: an ordinary rocky shell outside, a miniature crystal cave inside.

etymology.text: 英语早先用 greenhorn 指角尚幼嫩的动物，后来转指没有经验的人。把“刚长出嫩角”与“刚开始做事”联系起来。

usage_note: 非正式用语，可能带调侃或轻视；更中性的称呼可用 beginner 或 newcomer。

senses.meaning_zh: 新手；缺乏经验、容易受骗的人
senses.meaning_en: An inexperienced person, especially someone new to an activity or situation.
senses.english_definition: A greenhorn is someone who has little experience of a particular activity or situation and may therefore make mistakes or be easily deceived.
senses.collocation_en: a complete greenhorn; a greenhorn recruit
senses.collocation_zh: 一个完全没有经验的新手；一个初来乍到的新兵
senses.sentence_en: I was a complete greenhorn when I started working on the ranch.
senses.sentence_zh: 刚开始在牧场工作时，我是个完全没有经验的新手。

etymology_story.zh: 这个词早期用于指角尚未长成熟的幼牛，后来转指初入行、缺乏经验的人。green 在这里体现“尚未成熟”的含义，而非单纯表示颜色。
etymology_story.en: The word was used early on for a young ox whose horns had not fully developed, and it later came to mean an inexperienced person. Green conveys immaturity here rather than simply a colour.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：green（不成熟的、缺乏经验的）+ horn（角）→ greenhorn，属于复合名词。复数为 greenhorns；相关词有 green（缺乏经验的）和 greenness（不成熟；缺乏经验）。greenhorn 放在另一名词前通常是名词作定语，不必另立常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: green, meaning immature or inexperienced, + horn → greenhorn, a compound noun. The plural is greenhorns; related words include green, meaning inexperienced, and greenness, meaning immaturity or inexperience. Before another noun, greenhorn normally functions as a noun modifier rather than requiring a separate common adjective entry.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: novice（初学者）较中性，侧重经验或技能不足；rookie（新人、新兵）较口语化，常用于运动、军队和职场；beginner（初学者）只强调刚开始学习。greenhorn 常带调侃或轻微贬义，还可能暗示不懂世故、容易受骗。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Novice is relatively neutral and emphasizes limited experience or skill; rookie is informal and common in sports, military, and workplace contexts; beginner simply emphasizes that someone has just started learning. Greenhorn is often teasing or mildly disparaging and can suggest naivety or susceptibility to deception.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 角还没长成熟，经验也没长成熟：green + horn → 新手。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Undeveloped horns suggest undeveloped experience: green + horn → a newcomer.

pronunciation.note: 采用美式宽式 IPA；由词典的美式发音标记转写。

forms: 可数；复数 hyoids；更完整的名称是 hyoid bone。
family: hyoid bone 舌骨；hyoids 舌骨（复数）

morphology.text: hy-（希腊字母 upsilon 的名称成分）+ -oid（像……的）→ hyoid（形似字母U的）；名称来自形状，作名词时指舌骨。

etymology.text: 经新拉丁语 hyoides 进入英语，更早来自希腊语 hyoeidēs，意为“形似 upsilon 字母的”。看它的U形轮廓，就能把名字与形状对应起来。

usage_note: 本课为名词，相当于 hyoid bone；也可作形容词表示“舌骨的”。不要把它与甲状腺 thyroid 混淆。

senses.meaning_zh: 舌骨；位于舌根下方、支撑舌及相关肌肉的马蹄形骨
senses.meaning_en: A horseshoe-shaped bone below the tongue that supports the tongue and associated muscles.
senses.english_definition: The hyoid is a small horseshoe-shaped bone in the neck that supports the tongue and provides attachment points for muscles used in swallowing and speaking.
senses.collocation_en: fracture of the hyoid; the body of the hyoid
senses.collocation_zh: 舌骨骨折；舌骨体
senses.sentence_en: The hyoid provides attachment points for several muscles involved in swallowing.
senses.sentence_zh: 舌骨为数块参与吞咽的肌肉提供附着点。

senses.meaning_zh: 舌骨的；与舌骨有关的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to the hyoid bone.
senses.english_definition: Hyoid structures or movements are structures or movements associated with the hyoid bone.
senses.collocation_en: the hyoid bone; hyoid movement
senses.collocation_zh: 舌骨；舌骨运动
senses.sentence_en: Hyoid movement was recorded while the patient swallowed.
senses.sentence_zh: 记录了患者吞咽时的舌骨运动。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经拉丁语形式追溯到希腊语 hyoeidēs，意思是“形似字母 upsilon 的”。这一名称取自该骨的轮廓，与希腊大写字母 upsilon（Υ）的形状有关。
etymology_story.en: The word traces through Latin forms to Greek hyoeidēs, meaning shaped like the letter upsilon. The name refers to the bone's outline and its resemblance to the Greek capital letter upsilon, Υ.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜将 hyoid 作为整体解剖学词基；历史上包含表示 upsilon 的成分和表示“形似”的成分，不宜把 hy- 当作可自由使用的现代词根。复数为 hyoids；相关构词成分 hyo- 表示“舌骨”，词族包括 suprahyoid（舌骨上的）、infrahyoid（舌骨下的）、sternohyoid（胸骨舌骨肌；胸骨舌骨肌的）、thyrohyoid（甲状舌骨肌；甲状舌骨的）和 stylohyoid（茎突舌骨肌；茎突舌骨的）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, hyoid is best treated as an established anatomical base. Historically, it contains an element referring to upsilon and an element meaning resembling; hy- should not be presented as a freely productive modern root. The plural is hyoids. The related combining form hyo- means hyoid, as in suprahyoid, above the hyoid; infrahyoid, below it; sternohyoid, connecting the sternum and hyoid; thyrohyoid, connecting the thyroid cartilage and hyoid; and stylohyoid, connecting the styloid process and hyoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: hyoid bone（舌骨）是名词 hyoid 的标准完整名称；lingual bone（舌骨）是较少使用的同义名称，强调其与舌的关系。形容词 hyoid 通常用 relating to the hyoid bone（与舌骨有关的）解释，没有同样常用的单词同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Hyoid bone is the standard full equivalent of the noun hyoid; lingual bone is a less common alternative name emphasizing its relationship to the tongue. The adjective is normally paraphrased as relating to the hyoid bone and has no equally common single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 由字母形状记骨头轮廓：upsilon → 马蹄形舌骨。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect the letter shape to the bone's outline: upsilon → the horseshoe-shaped hyoid.

etymology.text: 现代英语将拉丁语来源的 multi-（多）与 stage 组合，形成表示多个阶段的形容词。想象一件事按几个连续步骤推进。

usage_note: 用于火箭、程序、处理过程等；多级火箭是各级推进装置依次工作，不是几个发动机始终同时工作。

etymology_story.zh: 这是英语用拉丁语来源的 multi-（多）与 stage（阶段、级）构成的透明复合词。stage 的历史意义涉及站立或展示的平台，后来发展出“进程中的一个阶段”等抽象含义。
etymology_story.en: This is a transparent English formation combining Latin-derived multi-, meaning many, with stage. Stage historically referred to a platform for standing or display and later developed abstract meanings such as a distinct phase in a process.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：multi-（多个）+ stage（阶段、级）→ multistage（多阶段的、多级的）；也写作 multi-stage。相关词族有 stage（阶段；安排、上演）、stages（阶段的复数；动词第三人称单数）、staged（分阶段安排的；上演了的）、staging（安排；上演）以及 single-stage（单阶段的、单级的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: multi-, meaning many, + stage → multistage, meaning involving several stages; multi-stage is an alternative spelling. Related forms include stage, a phase or the verb meaning arrange or present; stages, its plural or third-person singular verb; staged, its past form or an adjective meaning arranged in stages; staging, the act of arranging or presenting; and single-stage, involving one stage.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: multistep（多步骤的）强调多个具体操作；multiphase（多阶段的）强调多个时期或阶段，但在科学语境中也可指“多相的”；staged（分阶段进行的）强调有计划地分期实施。multistage 还特别适合描述具有多个工作级段的设备。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Multistep emphasizes several individual actions; multiphase emphasizes distinct phases, although in science it can also refer to multiple physical phases; staged emphasizes planned implementation in successive stages. Multistage is also especially suitable for equipment with several operating stages.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: multi- 是“多”，stage 是“阶段”：多个阶段接起来，就是 multistage。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Multi- means many and stage means a phase: several connected stages make something multistage.

etymology_story.zh: nitride 属于十九世纪形成的科学词汇，由表示氮的 nitr- 与化合物命名后缀 -ide 构成。其动词用法由名词发展而来，表示形成氮化物或进行渗氮处理。
etymology_story.en: Nitride belongs to nineteenth-century scientific vocabulary and combines nitr-, referring to nitrogen, with the compound-naming suffix -ide. The verb developed from the noun to describe forming nitrides or treating a material by nitriding.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：nitr-（氮）+ -ide（二元化合物命名后缀）→ nitride；名词可直接转作动词。词形有 nitrides（名词复数；动词第三人称单数）、nitrided（过去式、过去分词）和 nitriding（现在分词；渗氮处理）。相关词有 nitrogen（氮）、nitridation（氮化作用）和 carbonitriding（碳氮共渗）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: nitr-, referring to nitrogen, + -ide, a suffix used in naming binary compounds, → nitride; the noun also becomes a verb without an added suffix. Inflections are nitrides, the plural noun or third-person singular verb; nitrided, the past tense and past participle; and nitriding, the present participle or treatment process. Related terms include nitrogen, nitridation, meaning nitride formation, and carbonitriding, meaning treatment with both carbon and nitrogen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 名词 nitride 没有适用于所有语境的常用同义词：nitrogen compound（含氮化合物）范围更广，不能直接替换。动词方面，nitrogen-harden（通过渗氮硬化）突出处理目的；case-harden（表面硬化）范围更广，也包括渗碳等方法。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The noun nitride has no common synonym that works in every context: nitrogen compound is broader and is not an exact replacement. For the verb, nitrogen-harden emphasizes the hardening purpose; case-harden is broader and includes other methods, such as carburizing.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nitr- 锁定“氮”，-ide 提示“化合物”；把氮送进金属表面，就是动词 nitride。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Nitr- points to nitrogen and -ide signals a compound; putting nitrogen into a metal surface gives the verb nitride.

etymology_story.zh: sterol 在二十世纪初由 cholesterol（胆固醇）缩略形成，用来统称这一类甾体醇。更深层的来源涉及希腊语 stereos（固体的），而词尾 -ol 在化学命名中表示醇。
etymology_story.en: Sterol was formed in the early twentieth century by shortening cholesterol and became a general name for this class of steroid alcohols. Its deeper history involves Greek stereos, meaning solid, while the chemical ending -ol indicates an alcohol.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 sterol 是可独立使用的化学名词，也可作为复合词的词基；可以借 -ol 识别其“醇”的性质，但不宜把 ster- 当作意义完整的自由词。复数为 sterols；相关词族和类名包括 phytosterol（植物甾醇，phyto- + sterol）、zoosterol（动物甾醇，zoo- + sterol）、cholesterol（胆固醇）、ergosterol（麦角甾醇）、sitosterol（谷甾醇）和 stigmasterol（豆甾醇）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, sterol is an independent chemical noun and a base for compounds. The ending -ol helps identify its alcohol character, but ster- should not be treated as an independent word with a complete meaning. The plural is sterols. Related family terms and class members include phytosterol, a plant sterol formed from phyto- + sterol; zoosterol, an animal sterol formed from zoo- + sterol; cholesterol; ergosterol; sitosterol; and stigmasterol.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: steroid alcohol（甾体醇）是 sterol 的常见释义性近义表达；steroid（甾体）范围更广，许多甾体并非甾醇；cholesterol（胆固醇）是一种具体的甾醇，不能代表整个类别。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Steroid alcohol is a common explanatory equivalent of sterol; steroid is broader because many steroids are not sterols; cholesterol names one particular sterol and cannot stand for the whole class.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住 cholesterol 中的 sterol，再用 -ol 联想“醇”：胆固醇是甾醇家族的一员。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Spot sterol within cholesterol and connect -ol with alcohol: cholesterol is one member of the sterol family.

Its use subsequently extended to matting used in martial arts such as judo. [Etymological reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tatami)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是不可再分析的借入词：tatami，不拆成英语词根和词缀。可作可数名词，复数为 tatami 或 tatamis，也可集合地表示铺地席；常见复合形式有 tatami mat（榻榻米席）、tatami room（榻榻米房间）、tatami-covered（铺有榻榻米的）。没有常用的独立派生词族；在 tatami room 中作名词定语，不必另立形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, tatami is an unanalyzable loanword with no English root-and-affix division. Countable plurals are tatami and tatamis, and the word can also refer collectively to matting; common compounds include tatami mat, tatami room, and tatami-covered. It has no established family of common derivatives; its use before room is an attributive noun use.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rush mat（灯心草席）突出表面材料；straw mat（草席）是更宽泛的材料名称；martial arts mat（武术垫）强调运动用途。它们都不能在所有语境中替换具有日本文化特指性的 tatami。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rush mat emphasizes the woven surface material; straw mat is a broader material-based description; martial arts mat emphasizes sporting use. None is interchangeable with the culturally specific tatami in every context.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自意大利语 tiramisù，源于 tira mi su，字面意思是“把我拉起来”，也可理解为“让我振作起来”。这个表达成为甜点名称，英语用例至少可追溯到1982年。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tiramisu)
etymology_story.en: English borrowed Italian tiramisù, from tira mi su, literally 'pull me up' and idiomatically 'pick me up.' The expression became the dessert's name, with English use recorded from 1982. [Etymological reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tiramisu)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中作为整词借入，不按英语词根和词缀拆分；意大利语来源可分析为 tira（拉，命令式）+ mi（我）+ su（向上）。通常作不可数名词；表示多份或多种提拉米苏时可用复数 tiramisus。无常用的独立派生词族；tiramisu-like（像提拉米苏的）是可临时构造的形式，并非核心派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats tiramisu as a whole-word borrowing, without English roots or affixes; its Italian source contains tira ('pull,' imperative) + mi ('me') + su ('up'). It is usually uncountable, though tiramisus can refer to separate servings or varieties. It has no common established derivative family; tiramisu-like is a possible occasional formation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。coffee dessert（咖啡甜点）是上位描述；layered dessert（分层甜点）强调结构；coffee trifle（咖啡口味的英式分层甜点）是相近甜点，但配料和传统不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. Coffee dessert is a broader description; layered dessert describes its structure; coffee trifle names a related dessert with different ingredients and culinary traditions.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “让我振作起来”：把意大利语名称与一口咖啡味甜点带来的精神一振相连。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'pick me up': connect the Italian name with the lift you associate with a coffee-flavoured dessert.

etymology_story.zh: 经新拉丁语进入英语，源自希腊语 trachōma，意为“粗糙状态”，其基础词 trachys 意为“粗糙的”。名称指向患病时眼睑内侧结膜表面出现的粗糙变化。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/trachoma)
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through New Latin from Greek trachōma, meaning 'roughness,' based on trachys, 'rough.' The name refers to the roughened conjunctival surface inside affected eyelids. [Etymological reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/trachoma)

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代普通英语中主要作为完整病名使用；医学构词上可辨认 trach-（粗糙）和源自希腊语的 -oma（状态或病理形成物），此处 -oma 不表示肿瘤。主要派生词为 trachomatous（沙眼的；患沙眼的），构成为 trachomat-（派生词干）+ -ous（……的）。Chlamydia trachomatis 是相关病原体的学名，其中 trachomatis 是拉丁化屈折形式，不是普通英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In ordinary modern English, trachoma functions mainly as a complete disease name; medical analysis identifies trach- ('rough') and Greek-derived -oma ('condition or pathological formation'), which does not mean a tumour here. Its principal derivative is trachomatous ('relating to or affected by trachoma'), formed from trachomat- + -ous. Chlamydia trachomatis names the associated bacterium; trachomatis is a Latinized inflected form rather than an English derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: granular conjunctivitis（颗粒性结膜炎）和 Egyptian ophthalmia（埃及眼炎）是沙眼的历史名称，现代医学通常直接用 trachoma；conjunctivitis（结膜炎）是更宽泛的类别，不能等同于沙眼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Granular conjunctivitis and Egyptian ophthalmia are historical names for trachoma; modern medical usage generally prefers trachoma. Conjunctivitis is a broader category and does not specifically identify this disease.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: trach-＝“粗糙”：想到眼睑内侧变粗糙，扣住病名原义。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Trach- means 'rough': picture the roughened inner eyelid to connect the name with the disease.

etymology_story.zh: 英语借用新拉丁语植物属名 Trillium；据韦氏词典，该名称来自瑞典语 trilling，意为“三胞胎中的一个”，指植物的三片叶。它的“三”这一命名线索也便于联想到通常具有的三片花瓣。[词源参考：韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/trillium)
etymology_story.en: English adopted the New Latin genus name Trillium, which Merriam-Webster traces to Swedish trilling, 'triplet,' referring to the plant's three leaves. This three-part naming cue also recalls its typically three-petalled flower. [Etymological reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/trillium)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是完整的植物名称，不应硬拆成 trill（颤音）+ -ium。普通名词 trillium 的复数通常为 trilliums，也可用 trillia；植物属名写作首字母大写的 Trillium。无常用的独立派生词族；trillium-like（像延龄草的）是可临时构造的比较形式。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, trillium is a complete plant name, not trill ('a vibrating sound') + -ium. The common noun usually has the plural trilliums, with trillia also possible; the botanical genus name is capitalized as Trillium. It has no common established derivative family; trillium-like is a possible occasional comparison.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: wake-robin（延龄草的俗名）可指某些延龄草属植物；birthroot（延龄草的旧俗名）尤其与某些曾作药用的种类有关。这些俗名所指随地区和物种而变化，不能在精确植物分类中一概互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Wake-robin is a common name for certain trilliums; birthroot is an older name especially associated with some species formerly used medicinally. These names vary by region and species and are not universally interchangeable in precise botanical identification.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“三”：三片叶、三片花瓣；这是命名线索，不是把现代英语单词硬拆开。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Remember the pattern of three: three leaves and three petals. This recalls the naming logic without inventing an English morphological breakdown.

etymology_story.en: English formed ultramodern in the nineteenth century by adding Latin-derived ultra-, 'beyond,' to modern, giving the meaning 'extremely modern.' Recorded from 1833, it applies to areas including design, ideas, and lifestyles. [Historical usage reference: Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/ultramodern)

morphology_enriched.zh: ultra-（极度；超出）+ modern（现代的）→ ultramodern。直接相关形式包括 ultramodernism（极端现代主义）、ultramodernist（极端现代主义者；极端现代主义的），以及较少用的 ultramodernity（极端现代性）、ultramodernness（极其现代的性质）和 ultramodernly（以极其现代的方式）；基础词族还包括 modernity（现代性）、modernize/modernise（使现代化）、modernization/modernisation（现代化）、modernism（现代主义）、modernist（现代主义者；现代主义的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Ultra- ('extremely; beyond') + modern → ultramodern. Directly related forms include ultramodernism and ultramodernist, with less common formations ultramodernity, ultramodernness, and ultramodernly; the base family also includes modernity, modernize/modernise, modernization/modernisation, modernism, and modernist.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: state-of-the-art（采用当前最先进技术的）强调现有技术的最高水平；futuristic（未来风格的）强调像想象中的未来；cutting-edge（处于前沿的）强调创新领先。ultramodern 更概括地强调外观、观念或技术极其现代。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: State-of-the-art emphasizes the highest currently available technical standard; futuristic emphasizes resemblance to an imagined future; cutting-edge emphasizes leading innovation. Ultramodern more broadly stresses an extremely modern appearance, outlook, or technology.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ultra-＝“超出”：把 modern 的现代感推到极致。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ultra- means 'beyond': push modern to an extreme.

senses.meaning_zh: 生物标志物；可测量并反映生物过程、疾病状态或生物来源的特征或物质
senses.meaning_en: A measurable indicator of a biological process, condition, or origin

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学英语中由 bio-（生命、生物）与 marker（标记物、指示物）组成的复合词，其中 bio- 最终源自古希腊语 bíos（生命）。其用途涵盖医学中的生物状态指标，以及地球科学中指示生物来源的物质。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific compound combines bio-, ultimately from Ancient Greek bíos meaning 'life', with marker meaning an identifying sign or indicator. Its uses include indicators of biological conditions in medicine and substances indicating biological origins in earth science.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bio-（生物）+ marker（标记物）；marker = mark（标记）+ -er（执行某种作用的人或物）。复数为 biomarkers；相关词族有 mark（标记）、marked（有标记的）、marking（标记行为或标记）、marker（标记物）；biological marker（生物标志物）是对应的完整短语。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: bio- ('biological') + marker; marker itself consists of mark + -er, denoting an agent or instrument. The plural is biomarkers; related family members include mark, marked, marking, and marker. Biological marker is the corresponding expanded phrase.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: biological marker（生物标志物）是基本等义的完整形式；indicator（指标、指示物）适用范围更广，不限于生物学；marker（标志物）也更宽泛，通常依靠上下文确定其生物学含义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Biological marker is essentially the equivalent expanded form; indicator is broader and need not concern biology; marker is also broader and relies on context to establish a biological meaning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio 是生物，marker 是指示牌：身体或样本中可测量的“生物指示牌”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio means life; a marker points something out: a measurable sign of what is happening biologically.

etymology.text: 由德语 Bratwurst 借入英语，早期德语词中的肉与香肠组合，后来也让人联想到煎烤。想象烤架上的一根德式香肠。

etymology_story.zh: 英语直接借用了德语 Bratwurst，其历史形式中的前半部分指用于制作香肠的肉，后半部分 Wurst 意为“香肠”。前半部分后来常被联系到 braten（煎、烤），但不能简单把这种联想当作最初词源。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed German Bratwurst, whose historical first element referred to meat used for making sausages, while Wurst meant 'sausage'. The first element later became associated with braten, 'to fry or roast', but that association should not be mistaken for the original derivation.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中将 bratwurst 视为整体借词，不宜按英语词根和词缀拆分；德语内部可分析为 Brat-（历史上与制肠用肉有关）+ Wurst（香肠）。英语复数可用 bratwursts 或 bratwurst；美式口语常缩略为 brat（德式香肠），复数 brats。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, bratwurst is a whole-word borrowing rather than an English root-and-affix formation; within German, it contains Brat-, historically associated with sausage meat, and Wurst, 'sausage'. English plurals include bratwursts and unchanged bratwurst; the American informal clipping is brat, plural brats.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sausage（香肠）是上位词；frankfurter（法兰克福香肠）通常指质地细腻、经过熏制或熟制的另一类香肠；banger（香肠）是英式口语称呼，并不特指德式香肠。三者不能在强调具体品种时随意互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sausage is the general category; frankfurter usually denotes a different, finely textured sausage that is smoked or precooked; banger is an informal British term for a sausage and does not specifically identify bratwurst. These terms are not interchangeable when the variety matters.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 记住德语 Wurst 就是香肠，再把整词联结到烤架上的德式香肠。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor Wurst to 'sausage', then picture a German sausage sizzling on a grill.

etymology_story.zh: 英语经墨西哥西班牙语 cenote 借入此词，更早来自尤卡坦玛雅语 tsʼonoʼot，指有水的天然洞穴或深坑。这个地方性名称进入英语后，主要用于描述尤卡坦及类似石灰岩地区的此类地貌。
etymology_story.en: English acquired cenote through Mexican Spanish, ultimately from Yucatec Maya tsʼonoʼot, referring to a natural water-containing cavity or pit. The regional name entered English chiefly as a term for these features in Yucatán and comparable limestone landscapes.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 cenote 是不可进一步作常规词缀分析的整体借词；复数为 cenotes。可临时组合 cenote-like（像天然井的），其中 -like 表示“像……的”，但它不是常用的固定派生词；本词没有广泛使用的英语派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, cenote is an unanalyzed borrowing with the plural cenotes. Cenote-like can be formed productively with -like, meaning 'resembling', but it is not a common established derivative; the word has no widely used English derivational family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: water-filled sinkhole（积水的塌陷坑）是较接近的描述性表达；sinkhole（塌陷坑）范围更广，可以没有水；natural well（天然井）强调可见或可获取的地下水，并不限定相同的形成方式。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Water-filled sinkhole is a close descriptive equivalent; sinkhole is broader and may be dry; natural well emphasizes exposed or accessible groundwater without necessarily specifying the same formation process.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 石灰岩顶塌开，地下清水露出来：天然形成的一口井。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture limestone opening onto clear groundwater: nature has uncovered a well.

senses.meaning_zh: 协合式的；通过不同社会群体的代表合作并分享权力来治理的
senses.meaning_en: Relating to government through cooperation and power sharing among distinct social groups
senses.english_definition: A consociational political system allows representatives of different social groups to share power and cooperate in governing a divided society.
senses.collocation_en: consociational democracy; consociational power sharing
senses.collocation_zh: 协合式民主；协合式权力分享

senses.sentence_zh: 该协议确立了一种协合式体制，由主要社群共同分享行政权力。

etymology_story.zh: consociational 由 consociation（联合、结合）派生，后者可追溯至拉丁语 consociatio（联合），与表示“伙伴”的 socius 同源。它原有的“联合”含义后来在政治学中形成了更专门的用法，指社会群体通过代表合作与权力分享共同治理。
etymology_story.en: Consociational derives from consociation, 'association or union', ultimately from Latin consociatio and related to socius, 'companion'. Its general association-based meaning developed a specialized political use for government through cooperation and power sharing among representatives of distinct social groups.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代直接构词：consociation（联合）+ -al（……的）→ consociational。主要词族包括 consociate（联合；结成伙伴，少见）、consociation（联合；联合体）、consociationalism（协合主义；协合式治理理论）、consociationalist（协合主义者；协合主义的）和 non-consociational（非协合式的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Immediate modern formation: consociation + the adjective-forming suffix -al. Principal family members include the uncommon verb consociate, the noun consociation, consociationalism for the political theory or system, consociationalist for an advocate or a related adjective, and non-consociational.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: power-sharing（权力分享的）最接近，但涵盖的安排比协合式治理更广；consensual（共识型的）强调通过广泛同意作决策，不一定按社群分配权力；coalition-based（以联合执政为基础的）强调联盟执政，也不必具有稳定的社群代表机制。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Power-sharing is the closest broader term; consensual emphasizes decision-making through broad agreement without necessarily allocating power among communities; coalition-based emphasizes government by an alliance without necessarily establishing durable representation for distinct social groups.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 从“联合”想到“共同执政”：不同社群各有代表，一起分享治理权。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect association with shared government: distinct communities send representatives to govern together.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从法语 courant（奔跑的）借入此词；它是 courir（跑）的现在分词形式，最终源自拉丁语 currere（跑）。在英语纹章学中，该词保留了描述动物奔跑姿态的专门含义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed French courant, 'running', the present participle of courir, ultimately from Latin currere, 'to run'. English heraldry preserves this specialized use for the running posture of an animal.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 courant 是整体借入的形容词，不应将其末尾 -ant 当作英语中临时添加的后缀。纹章学复合形式 counter-courant 表示动物朝相反方向奔跑；current（当前的；水流）与其有历史词源联系，但不是由英语 courant 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, courant is a borrowed adjective rather than a formation created by adding English -ant. The heraldic compound counter-courant describes animals running in opposite directions; current is historically related but is not a direct English derivative of courant.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: running（奔跑的）是普通英语中的释义性对应词；salient（跃起的）和 rampant（以后腿支撑、前身昂起的）是相关的纹章姿态术语，并非同义词，分别强调跳跃和直立昂起的姿势。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Running is the ordinary-English descriptive equivalent; salient and rampant are related heraldic posture terms rather than synonyms: salient indicates leaping, while rampant indicates an upright posture supported on the hind legs.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：cow（牛）+ bird（鸟）→ cowbird，属于名词加名词的复合词。复数为 cowbirds；没有常用的独立派生词，brown-headed cowbird“褐头牛鹂”等属于物种名称。

etymology_story.zh: 英语借自西班牙语 criollo，后者源于葡萄牙语 crioulo，并最终与表示“养育、繁育”的动词 criar 有关。这个词原先强调殖民地本地出生或养育，后来既用于特定历史人群，也用于当地发展的马、可可等。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed criollo from Spanish, which took it from Portuguese crioulo, ultimately related to criar, meaning 'to raise or breed.' Its association with local birth or upbringing in a colony developed into uses for historical populations and locally developed horses, cacao, and other products.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 criollo 是整体借入的词，通常不拆成英语词根和词缀；名词复数为 criollos，形容词不变。相关形式有 criolla（西班牙语阴性形式，也见于借入表达）、criollismo（克里奥尔文化或文学倾向的借词）及较少见的 criollism；creole 是同源词，不是它的英语派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, criollo is a borrowed base rather than a combination of productive English roots and affixes; its noun plural is criollos, and its adjective is unchanged. Related forms include criolla, the Spanish feminine form found in borrowed expressions, criollismo, a borrowing for a cultural or literary movement, and the less common criollism; creole is a cognate, not an English derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: creole“克里奥尔人／克里奥尔的”在部分历史语境中最接近，但各地区含义不同，也可涉及语言；native-born“本地出生的”只说明出生地，不限定血统；locally bred“本地培育的”适用于马等动物，不表示历史社会身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Creole is the closest equivalent in some historical contexts, but its meanings vary by region and also extend to languages. Native-born specifies birthplace without ancestry, while locally bred suits animals such as horses without implying a historical social identity.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 核心是“在当地养育、长成”：欧洲血统可在美洲出生，马和可可也可在当地发展。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to 'raised locally': people can be locally born, and horses or cacao can develop into local types.

etymology_story.en: Deadbolt combines dead, in the sense of inactive, with bolt, meaning a locking bar. The name emphasizes a bolt that must be moved directly rather than one operated by a spring.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dead（不自行活动的）+ bolt（锁舌）→ deadbolt；名词可零派生为动词。词族及屈折形式：deadbolts（名词复数或动词第三人称单数）、deadbolted（过去式、过去分词）、deadbolting（现在分词）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: dead + bolt → deadbolt; the noun also becomes a verb through conversion without an added suffix. The family and inflections include deadbolts, deadbolted, and deadbolting.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: deadlock 在门锁语境中可作近义词，但也常表示“僵局”；bolt“门闩、锁舌”范围更广；latch“碰锁、门扣”通常指可随关门动作扣合的装置，与 deadbolt 的机构不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Deadlock can be a synonym in the context of door hardware, although it also means an impasse. Bolt is broader, while latch usually refers to a fastening that can catch as the door closes and uses a different mechanism.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dead + bolt：锁舌不会自己弹动，要转动钥匙或旋钮。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dead + bolt: the bolt stays put until you turn the key or knob.

etymology_story.zh: deadfall 是 dead 与 fall 组成的本土复合词，历史上较早用于落下重物、将猎物压死的陷阱。它也用于林中倒下的枯木，这一义项可直接按“枯死后倒下的东西”理解。
etymology_story.en: Deadfall is a native English compound of dead and fall, historically used for a trap whose falling weight kills its prey. It also denotes fallen dead timber, a sense readily understood as dead material that has fallen.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：dead（死的、致死的）+ fall（落下）→ deadfall。表示捕兽陷阱时通常可数，复数为 deadfalls；表示林地倒木时常作集合性不可数名词；没有常用的独立派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: dead + fall → deadfall. The trap sense is normally countable, with the plural deadfalls; the fallen-timber sense is often a collective mass noun, and there are no established common derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: falling-weight trap“落重式陷阱”明确对应捕兽义；fallen timber“倒木”对应林地木材义，但不一定原先已枯死；windthrow“风倒木”特指被风吹倒或连根掀倒的树木。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Falling-weight trap explicitly matches the trapping sense. Fallen timber matches the woodland sense without necessarily implying prior death, while windthrow specifically refers to trees blown down or uprooted by wind.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: dead + fall：枯木倒下；重物落下也能致死。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Dead + fall: dead wood falls, and a falling weight can kill.

etymology_story.zh: deglaze 在英语构词上是 de-“去除”加 glaze“釉层、光亮覆层”。其烹饪义受到法语 déglacer 的影响；法语词字面意为“去冰”，在烹饪中指加入液体化开锅底残留物。
etymology_story.en: Deglaze is formed in English from de-, meaning removal, and glaze, meaning a glossy coating. Its culinary use was influenced by French déglacer, literally 'to remove ice,' which in cooking means adding liquid to release deposits from a pan.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：de-（去除、逆转）+ glaze（覆以釉层或光亮层）→ deglaze。词族及屈折形式：deglazes、deglazed、deglazing（加 -ing 时去掉词尾不发音的 e）；相关名词 deglazer 指去釉或去光剂，基础词族还包括 glaze、glazed、glazing。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern structure: de- + glaze → deglaze. Family members and inflections include deglazes, deglazed, and deglazing, with the final silent e dropped before -ing; deglazer names a product that removes a surface finish, and the base family includes glaze, glazed, and glazing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: loosen“使松脱”强调让锅底残留物脱离表面；dissolve“溶解”强调进入液体，但不是所有残留物都会完全溶解；strip“剥除”更接近去除涂层的技术义，范围也更广。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Loosen emphasizes releasing deposits from the pan, while dissolve emphasizes their entering the liquid, although not every deposit fully dissolves. Strip is closer to the technical coating-removal sense and has a broader range of uses.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: de- 去掉 + glaze 覆层：让表面那一层脱离；烹饪时把锅底的香味带进汁里。
mnemonic_anchor.en: De- removes a glaze-like layer: in cooking, release the flavorful layer from the pan into the sauce.

senses.meaning_zh: 底栖的；近底层的，指生活或活动在海底、湖底附近的鱼类等动物

etymology_story.zh: 源自拉丁语 demersus，意为“沉入水中的”，是 demergere（使沉没）的过去分词；英语加上形容词后缀 -al。在水生生物学中，它发展为表示“生活或活动在水底附近的”。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin demersus, meaning 'submerged', the past participle of demergere, 'to sink', with the adjective suffix -al. In aquatic biology, it came to describe animals living or feeding near the bottom.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词结构：demers-（来自拉丁语、表示“沉入水中”的词干）+ -al（形容词后缀）。现代英语通常将 demersal 作为完整术语使用；相关副词 demersally（以近底层方式）较少见，demersal fish 是词组而非派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Structure: demers- (a Latin-derived stem meaning 'submerged') + -al (an adjective suffix). Modern English generally treats demersal as a complete technical term; the related adverb demersally is uncommon, and demersal fish is a phrase rather than a derivative.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: benthic（底栖的）侧重水底生态环境及其生物；bottom-dwelling（生活在底部的）是直白的描述；demersal 尤常描述在水底附近活动、觅食的鱼类，不一定直接附着或生活在底质上。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Benthic emphasizes the bottom habitat and its organisms; bottom-dwelling is a plain descriptive alternative. Demersal is especially common for fish moving or feeding near the bottom, without necessarily living directly on the substrate.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: “沉下去”→ 靠近水底生活：demersal。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Think 'sunk down' → living near the bottom: demersal.

etymology_story.zh: ditz 是美国非正式英语词，通常被认为由形容词 ditzy 或 ditsy（糊涂健忘的）逆构而来。形容词本身更早的来源并不确定，不能据此虚构一个表示“糊涂”的古代词根。
etymology_story.en: Ditz is an informal American word generally understood as a back-formation from ditzy or ditsy, meaning 'scatterbrained'. The adjective's earlier origin is uncertain, so no established ancient root meaning 'confusion' should be assumed.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代词族可分析为 ditz（糊涂虫）+ -y → ditzy（糊涂健忘的）；ditzy 去掉词尾 y 再加 -iness → ditziness（糊涂健忘）。异体为 ditsy、ditsiness；名词复数为 ditzes。这个便于学习的构词方向不代表实际历史顺序，历史上通常认为形容词先于名词。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern word-family learning: ditz + -y → ditzy; replacing the final y with -iness gives ditziness. Variant spellings are ditsy and ditsiness, and the noun plural is ditzes. This learning pattern does not represent the usual historical account, in which the adjective preceded the noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: scatterbrain（粗心健忘的人）突出注意力分散；airhead（没头脑的人）更强调缺乏思考、常更具侮辱性；space cadet（神游的人）突出心不在焉、脱离眼前情境。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Scatterbrain emphasizes absent-mindedness and poor concentration; airhead stresses a lack of serious thought and is often more insulting; space cadet emphasizes seeming mentally elsewhere or out of touch with the immediate situation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: ditzy 是“糊涂的”，ditz 就是“那个糊涂的人”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Ditzy describes the behavior; a ditz is the person showing it.

etymology_story.zh: 源自古希腊语 epistaxis，表示“滴流”，尤其指鼻出血，与 epistazein（滴落）有关。英语医学沿用了它指鼻出血的专门含义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from ancient Greek epistaxis, meaning 'dripping', especially bleeding from the nose, and is related to epistazein, 'to drip'. Medical English retained its specialized meaning of nasal bleeding.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中宜整体识记，不把它当作能自由组合的英语前后缀词。历史结构可解释为 epi-（在……上、向……）+ stag-/staz-（滴）+ 动作名词后缀 -sis，组合时形成 -staxis；古典式复数为 epistaxes，日常医学用法通常将其视为不可数名词，没有常用的现代派生词族。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, learn it as a whole term rather than as freely combinable English affixes. Historically, it contains epi- ('upon' or 'toward'), stag-/staz- ('drip'), and the action-noun suffix -sis, producing the form -staxis. The classical plural is epistaxes, but ordinary medical usage generally treats epistaxis as uncountable, with no common modern derivative family.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: nosebleed 是日常表达，可指一次鼻出血；nasal bleeding 是透明、描述性的表达；epistaxis 是病历和医学讨论中的正式术语，三者核心所指相同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Nosebleed is the everyday term and can refer to a single episode; nasal bleeding is a transparent descriptive expression; epistaxis is the formal term used in clinical records and medical discussion. Their central reference is the same.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 词源中的“滴流”→ 鼻孔滴血 → 鼻出血。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Historical 'dripping' → blood dripping from the nose → epistaxis.

etymology_story.zh: 来自意大利解剖学家 Bartolomeo Eustachi 的姓氏，其拉丁化形式为 Eustachius。英语将其构成纪念性形容词，用于咽鼓管、下腔静脉瓣等解剖结构的名称。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from the surname of the Italian anatomist Bartolomeo Eustachi, Latinized as Eustachius. English formed an commemorative adjective used in names for anatomical structures such as the auditory tube and the valve of the inferior vena cava.

morphology_enriched.zh: 可按人名词干 Eustachi- + 形容词后缀 -an 理解，是人名派生形容词，不宜再拆成具有普通词义的英语词根。没有常用的进一步派生词族；Eustachian tube 和 Eustachian valve 是术语词组，医学文献中也常见小写形式 eustachian。
morphology_enriched.en: It can be understood as the personal-name stem Eustachi- + the adjective suffix -an. It is an adjective derived from a name, not a combination of ordinary English meaning-bearing roots. There is no common further derivative family; Eustachian tube and Eustachian valve are technical phrases, and lowercase eustachian is also common in medical writing.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 该形容词没有通用的单词级近义词。在 Eustachian tube 中，整个词组可换为 auditory tube（听管）或 pharyngotympanic tube（咽鼓管）；后者更直接说明它连接咽部与鼓室，这两个表达不适用于 Eustachian valve。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: The adjective has no general single-word synonym. The complete phrase Eustachian tube can be replaced by auditory tube or pharyngotympanic tube; the latter more explicitly identifies its connection between the pharynx and tympanic cavity. Neither expression replaces Eustachian in Eustachian valve.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Eustachi 是人名；Eustachian 表示“以他命名的”，常见于咽鼓管。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Eustachi is the person; Eustachian means 'named after him', especially in Eustachian tube.

etymology_story.zh: 由国际单位制前缀 giga-（十亿，词源与希腊语表示“巨人”的词有关）和频率单位 hertz 组成。hertz 为纪念德国物理学家 Heinrich Hertz 而命名，两者结合后表示每秒十亿个周期。
etymology_story.en: Gigahertz combines the SI prefix giga-, meaning 'one billion' and ultimately related to the Greek word for 'giant', with hertz. Hertz was named in honor of the German physicist Heinrich Hertz, so the combined unit represents one billion cycles per second.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：giga-（10⁹）+ hertz（赫兹）。单复数同形，单位符号为 GHz；同系列单位包括 hertz（赫兹）、kilohertz（千赫兹）、megahertz（兆赫兹）和 terahertz（太赫兹），它们是平行构成的单位名称，并非 gigahertz 的派生词。用于 gigahertz frequencies 等结构时属于名词作定语，无须另列形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: giga- (10⁹) + hertz. Singular and plural have the same form, and the unit symbol is GHz. Related unit names include hertz, kilohertz, megahertz, and terahertz; these are parallel formations rather than derivatives of gigahertz. In expressions such as gigahertz frequencies, the word is an attributive noun, so a separate adjective entry is unnecessary.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: GHz 是 gigahertz 的单位符号；one billion hertz（十亿赫兹）和 one thousand megahertz（一千兆赫兹）都与 one gigahertz（一吉赫兹）精确相等。这些是同一频率量值的不同写法，而非存在语义强弱差别的普通近义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: GHz is the unit symbol for gigahertz. One billion hertz and one thousand megahertz are both exactly equivalent to one gigahertz. These are alternative representations of the same frequency value, rather than ordinary synonyms with differences in emphasis.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: giga- 是十亿，hertz 是每秒周期数：1 GHz = 每秒十亿个周期。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Giga- means one billion; hertz counts cycles per second: 1 GHz = one billion cycles per second.

etymology_story.zh: 英语通过法语借入这一奶酪名称，名称来自瑞士的格鲁耶尔地区及当地城镇 Gruyères。它原本是产地名称，后来成为当地传统奶酪的名称；英语也常写作 Gruyère。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the cheese name from French, where it refers to the Gruyère region and the town of Gruyères in Switzerland. The geographical name became the name of the region’s traditional cheese; the spelling Gruyère is also common in English.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中是整体借词 gruyere，通常写作 Gruyère，不能拆成有意义的英语词根和词缀。通常作不可数名词；Gruyeres 可用于表示不同品种或不同批次。没有常用的派生词族；Gruyere-like（类似格鲁耶尔奶酪的）是可临时构成的形容词，并非常用独立词条。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, gruyere, often written Gruyère, is an unanalysed loanword with no productive English root-and-affix breakdown. It is normally uncountable; Gruyeres can refer to varieties or individual cheeses. It has no established everyday derivative family; Gruyere-like is a possible descriptive formation rather than a common independent dictionary word.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有严格同义词。近似品类词包括 Emmental（埃门塔尔奶酪，通常有明显的大孔洞）、Comté（孔泰奶酪，法国的相关硬质奶酪）和 Beaufort（博福尔奶酪，法国阿尔卑斯地区的相关奶酪）；这些名称各指不同奶酪，不能直接等同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact synonym. Related cheeses include Emmental, typically distinguished by large holes; Comté, a related French firm cheese; and Beaufort, a related cheese from the French Alps. These names identify different cheeses and are not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 地名变食名：Gruyères 的奶酪，就是 Gruyère。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Place becomes food: cheese from Gruyères gives you Gruyère.

senses.meaning_zh: 异养的；利用现成有机物作为碳源的
senses.meaning_en: Using existing organic compounds as a source of carbon.
senses.english_definition: A heterotrophic organism obtains the carbon it needs from existing organic substances rather than making all its organic material from carbon dioxide.

etymology_story.zh: 这是现代科学词汇，由源自希腊语的 hetero-（其他、不同）和与 trophē（营养、滋养）相关的 -trophic 构成。其生物学含义是依赖现成的有机碳，常与 autotrophic（自养的）相对。
etymology_story.en: This modern scientific formation combines Greek-derived hetero-, meaning 'other' or 'different', with -trophic, related to Greek trophē, meaning 'nourishment'. In biology, it describes dependence on pre-existing organic carbon and commonly contrasts with autotrophic.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：hetero-（其他、不同）+ -trophic（与营养方式有关的）→ heterotrophic（异养的）。主要词族：heterotroph（异养生物，名词）、heterotrophs（复数）、heterotrophy（异养，名词）、heterotrophically（以异养方式，副词）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: hetero- ('other, different') + -trophic ('relating to nutrition') → heterotrophic. The principal family comprises heterotroph, the noun for an organism; heterotrophs, its plural; heterotrophy, the nutritional mode; and heterotrophically, the adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: organic-carbon-dependent（依赖有机碳的）最直接地说明其碳源；non-autotrophic（非自养的）侧重否定自养能力。两者都是解释性近义表达；heterotrophic 是更规范的生物学术语，其核心区别在于碳源，而不只是能量来源。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Organic-carbon-dependent directly identifies the carbon source, while non-autotrophic emphasizes the absence of autotrophic nutrition. Both are explanatory near-equivalents; heterotrophic is the standard biological term, and its central distinction concerns carbon source rather than simply energy source.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hetero-＝别的，-trophic＝营养：有机碳从别处来。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hetero- means 'other' and -trophic concerns nutrition: organic carbon comes from elsewhere.

senses.meaning_zh: 高超声速的；通常指速度达到或超过五倍音速的

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 hyper-（超过、极度）与 sonic（声音的）构成，sonic 最终源自拉丁语 sonus（声音）。它在20世纪航空研究中成为专门术语，用来指称远高于音速的飞行状态。
etymology_story.en: The word combines hyper-, meaning 'beyond' or 'extremely', with sonic, which ultimately derives from Latin sonus, meaning 'sound'. It became a technical term in twentieth-century aeronautics for flight far above the speed of sound.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：hyper-（超过、极度）+ sonic（声音的）→ hypersonic（高超声速的）；更深层可分析为 son-（声音）+ -ic（形容词后缀）。主要词族：hypersonically（以高超声速，副词）、hypersonics（高超声速研究或技术，名词）；相关基础词包括 sonic（声音的）和 sonically（在声音方面）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: hyper- ('beyond, extremely') + sonic ('relating to sound') → hypersonic; sonic can be further related to son- ('sound') + -ic, an adjective suffix. Principal derivatives are hypersonically and hypersonics, the field or technology of hypersonic flight; related base-family forms include sonic and sonically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: supersonic（超声速的）泛指超过音速，范围比 hypersonic 更广；high-speed（高速的）和 ultrafast（极快的）只是一般速度描述，没有五倍音速这一技术门槛。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Supersonic covers speeds above the speed of sound and is broader than hypersonic. High-speed and ultrafast describe great speed in general and carry no specific Mach 5 threshold.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: hyper- 把 sonic 的速度推得更高：想到五倍音速门槛。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Hyper- pushes sonic much further: picture the Mach 5 threshold.

etymology_story.zh: 英语从意第绪语 klots 借入此词，其字面意思是“木块、木头”，也可比喻笨拙的人。这种从不灵活的木块到笨拙人物的比喻保留在英语口语中，既可用于自嘲，也可带贬义。
etymology_story.en: English borrowed the word from Yiddish klots, literally 'a block or log of wood', also used figuratively for an awkward person. The image of an unresponsive block survives in informal English, where the word can be self-mocking or insulting.

morphology_enriched.zh: klutz 是整体借入的名词，现代英语中不再拆分。主要词族及变化：klutzes（名词复数）；klutz + -y → klutzy（笨拙的）；klutzier、klutziest（比较级、最高级）；klutzily（笨拙地）；klutziness（笨拙）。
morphology_enriched.en: Klutz is a borrowed noun with no further productive internal breakdown in English. Its principal forms and derivatives are klutzes, the plural; klutz + -y → klutzy; klutzier and klutziest, the comparative and superlative; klutzily, the adverb; and klutziness, the quality noun.

synonyms_and_nuances.en: Butterfingers particularly suggests dropping things; bungler emphasizes doing a task badly; and oaf may additionally suggest rough manners or dullness. Klutz most often focuses on physical clumsiness.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 像块木头一样不灵活：klutz 就是笨手笨脚的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture someone moving like a block of wood: a klutz is physically awkward.

senses.meaning_zh: 超大城市；通常指人口至少一千万的城市集聚区
senses.meaning_en: A very large urban agglomeration, usually with at least ten million inhabitants.

etymology_story.zh: 该词由 mega-（巨大）和 city（城市）构成，其中 mega- 源自希腊语 megas（大的）。随着城市规模扩大，它被用于描述人口极为集中的城市地区，后来在城市与人口研究中常与一千万人口这一门槛联系起来。
etymology_story.en: The word combines mega-, meaning 'very large' and derived from Greek megas, with city. As cities expanded, it came to describe exceptionally populous urban areas and became commonly associated in urban and population studies with a ten-million-person threshold.

morphology_enriched.zh: 构词公式：mega-（巨大的）+ city（城市）→ megacity（超大城市）；这里的 mega- 表示规模巨大，并非严格表示“一百万”。复数为 megacities，遵循辅音字母加 y 变为 -ies 的规则；没有常用的专属派生词族。基础词 city 的相关构词包括 citywide（全市的／地）和 cityscape（城市景观）。
morphology_enriched.en: Formation: mega- ('very large') + city → megacity; mega- is an intensifier here, not a literal multiplier of one million. The plural is megacities, following the consonant-plus-y to -ies rule; there is no established everyday derivative family specific to megacity. Related formations from city include citywide and cityscape.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: metropolis（大都市）强调城市的重要性及中心地位，没有固定人口门槛；megalopolis（巨型城市带）通常指多个大都市地区相连形成的区域；conurbation（连片城市区）强调原本分开的城镇扩展后连成一片。megacity 主要强调人口规模。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Metropolis emphasizes a city's size and importance without a fixed population threshold. Megalopolis usually describes an extensive region of connected metropolitan areas, while conurbation emphasizes settlements that have expanded and joined together. Megacity primarily emphasizes population size.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: mega-＝巨大，city＝城市：人口多到千万级。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mega- means huge, city means city: picture an urban population in the tens of millions.

etymology_story.zh: “无角”义源于凯尔特语，与爱尔兰语和苏格兰盖尔语 maol（秃的、无角的）同源，英语中至少见于19世纪。北美口语中的“骡鹿”义与 mule deer 这一名称相联系，不能据此推断该动物无角。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/muley)；[蒙大拿州野生动物部门用例](https://fwp.mt.gov/hunt/regulations/deer)
etymology_story.en: The hornless sense is of Celtic origin, related to Irish and Scottish Gaelic maol, meaning bald or hornless, and is recorded in nineteenth-century English. The informal North American mule-deer sense is associated with the name mule deer and does not imply that the deer lacks antlers. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/muley); [Montana FWP usage](https://fwp.mt.gov/hunt/regulations/deer)

morphology_enriched.zh: 无角义在现代英语中宜作整词处理，不宜分析成 mule（骡子）加后缀，也不宜把盖尔语词形直接当作现代英语词根。形容词可转作可数名词，复数为 muleys；“骡鹿”义可联系 mule deer 理解，但属于另一语义来源。常见拼写变体有 mooly；无常用的进一步派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: For the hornless sense, treat muley as a whole lexical item rather than as mule plus a suffix or as a productive English formation from a Gaelic root. The adjective also functions as a count noun, with plural muleys; the mule-deer sense can be associated with mule deer but has a separate semantic basis. Mooly is a spelling variant; there are no common further derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: polled（天生无角的）是畜牧语境中更标准、技术性更强的近义词；hornless（无角的）含义更宽，不一定强调天生如此。名词 mule deer（骡鹿）对应其北美口语动物名称义，与“无角牛”义不同。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Polled is the more standard livestock term for naturally hornless animals; hornless is broader and need not specify that the condition is natural. Mule deer is the standard equivalent of the informal wildlife noun sense, which is distinct from the hornless-cow sense.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 分两幅图记：maol 的“秃头”联想无角牛；mule deer 的大耳朵联想骡鹿。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two pictures: maol's bare head suggests a hornless cow; mule deer's large ears suggest the informal deer name.

etymology_story.zh: Naproxen 是20世纪形成的药物通用名，由 naphthyl（萘基）、propionic acid（丙酸）、oxy（氧）及药名结尾 -en 的成分压缩组合而成。其名称反映化学结构，英语用例至少可追溯至1971年。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/naproxen)
etymology_story.en: Naproxen is a twentieth-century generic drug name formed by compressing elements of naphthyl, propionic acid, oxy, and the drug-name ending -en. Its name reflects its chemical structure and is recorded in English from at least 1971. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/naproxen)

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代用法中是不可数的药物名称，宜整词识记；历史命名可表示为 naphthyl + propionic acid + oxy + -en → naproxen，但这些成分经过缩合，并非可逐段对应的普通词根加词缀。无常用的形容词、动词或副词派生形式；naproxen sodium（萘普生钠）是相关盐类名称，naproxen-containing（含萘普生的）是临时构成的复合修饰语。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern usage, naproxen is an uncountable drug name best learned as a whole. Its historical naming formula is naphthyl + propionic acid + oxy + -en → naproxen, with compression rather than a transparent root-and-affix structure. It has no common adjective, verb, or adverb derivatives; naproxen sodium names a related salt, and naproxen-containing is a freely formed compound modifier.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无常用普通词汇近义词。Naprosyn 是含萘普生制剂使用的商品名；naproxen sodium（萘普生钠）是其钠盐，名称不应与游离酸完全混同；ibuprofen（布洛芬）属于同类非甾体抗炎药，但不是同一种药物。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common ordinary-language synonym. Naprosyn is a brand name used for naproxen preparations; naproxen sodium is its sodium salt and should be distinguished from the free acid; ibuprofen belongs to the same broad NSAID class but is a different drug.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: nap- 联想 naphthyl（萘基）：名称开头的“萘”连接药名“萘普生”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link nap- with naphthyl: the naphthalene-related fragment anchors the name naproxen.

etymology_story.zh: 该词于19世纪经新拉丁语医学术语进入英语，由希腊语来源的 osteo-（骨）、myel-（骨髓）和 -itis（炎症）组成。其字面结构突出骨与骨髓，现代临床用法通常指感染引起的骨组织炎症。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/osteomyelitis)；[美国国家癌症研究所](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/osteomyelitis)
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through New Latin medical terminology in the nineteenth century, combining Greek-derived elements for bone, marrow, and inflammation. Its structure highlights bone and marrow, while modern clinical usage usually concerns inflammation of bone caused by infection. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/osteomyelitis); [National Cancer Institute](https://www.cancer.gov/publications/dictionaries/cancer-terms/def/osteomyelitis)

morphology_enriched.zh: osteo-（骨）+ myel-（骨髓）+ -itis（炎症）→ osteomyelitis（骨髓炎）；也可按 osteo- + myelitis 分析，但独立词 myelitis 在现代医学中通常指脊髓炎。直接派生形容词为 osteomyelitic（骨髓炎的）；该名词通常不可数，专门文献中可见复数 osteomyelitides。相关同根词有 osteitis（骨炎）、myelitis（脊髓炎）和 osteomyelopathy（骨髓病）。
morphology_enriched.en: osteo- (bone) + myel- (marrow) + -itis (inflammation) → osteomyelitis. It can also be analyzed as osteo- + myelitis, although independent myelitis usually means inflammation of the spinal cord in modern medicine. The direct adjective is osteomyelitic; the noun is usually uncountable, with the specialist plural osteomyelitides. Related formations include osteitis, myelitis, and osteomyelopathy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: bone infection（骨感染）是常用通俗近似表达，但强调感染而非炎症。osteitis（骨炎）范围较宽，不一定涉及骨髓或感染；myelitis（脊髓炎）通常指脊髓炎症，不能因 myel- 的共同词源而当作同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Bone infection is the usual plain-language near-equivalent, emphasizing infection rather than inflammation. Osteitis is broader and need not involve marrow or infection; myelitis usually concerns the spinal cord and is not a synonym despite the shared historical element.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 骨 osteo- ＋ 骨髓 myel- ＋ 发炎 -itis：骨与骨髓发炎。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bone + marrow + inflammation: read the word as a map of the affected tissue and condition.

senses.meaning_en: A developing planetary body in the early stages of planet formation.

etymology_story.zh: Protoplanet 是20世纪天文学英语中形成的词，由希腊语来源的 proto-（最初的、早期的）与 planet（行星）组合，英语记录至少可追溯至1949年。该名称把行星形成过程中的早期天体称作“初期行星”。[韦氏词典](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/protoplanet)；[美国航空航天局术语表](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/glossary/)
etymology_story.en: Protoplanet was formed in twentieth-century astronomical English from Greek-derived proto-, meaning first or early, and planet, with English records dating to at least 1949. The name identifies an early planetary body within the process of planet formation. [Merriam-Webster](https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/protoplanet); [NASA glossary](https://science.nasa.gov/universe/glossary/)

morphology_enriched.zh: proto-（初期的）+ planet（行星）→ protoplanet（原行星）；复数为 protoplanets。直接相关形容词为 protoplanetary（原行星的；与行星形成早期有关的），常见于 protoplanetary disk（原行星盘）；基础词族包括 planet（行星）和 planetary（行星的）。无常用的直接动词或副词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: proto- (early) + planet → protoplanet; plural protoplanets. The related adjective is protoplanetary, meaning associated with protoplanets or early planet formation, as in protoplanetary disk. The base family includes planet and planetary. There are no common direct verb or adverb derivatives.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: planetary embryo（行星胚胎）常作近义表达，但不同形成模型对阶段的划分可能不同；developing planet（正在形成的行星）是较宽泛的通俗表达。planetesimal（星子）通常指更小的行星构成体，不宜直接等同于原行星。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Planetary embryo is often a near-synonym, although models may distinguish developmental stages; developing planet is a broader plain-language expression. A planetesimal is generally a smaller planetary building block and should not automatically be treated as equivalent.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: proto-＝初期：把 protoplanet 想成仍在成长的“行星幼体”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Proto- means early: picture a planetary youngster still gathering material and growing.

senses.meaning_zh: 精神药理学，研究药物如何影响心理、情绪和行为的学科
senses.meaning_en: The scientific study of how drugs affect mental processes, emotions, and behavior.

senses.collocation_en: clinical psychopharmacology; research in psychopharmacology

senses.sentence_zh: 她的精神药理学研究探讨药物如何影响记忆。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于20世纪初由 psycho-（心理、精神）与 pharmacology（药理学）组合形成；更深层的希腊语成分分别与“心灵”“药物”和“研究”有关。它逐渐成为研究药物对心理与行为影响的学科名称。[柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/psychopharmacology)；[美国心理学会词典](https://dictionary.apa.org/psychopharmacology)
etymology_story.en: The term was formed in the early twentieth century from psycho-, referring to the mind, and pharmacology; its deeper Greek elements concern mind, drugs, and study. It became the name of the discipline investigating drugs' effects on psychological processes and behavior. [Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/us/dictionary/english/psychopharmacology); [APA Dictionary](https://dictionary.apa.org/psychopharmacology)

morphology_enriched.zh: psycho-（心理、精神）+ pharmacology（药理学）→ psychopharmacology；进一步可分为 psycho- + pharmaco-（药物）+ -logy（学科、研究）。主要直接词族：psychopharmacologist（精神药理学家）、psychopharmacologic／psychopharmacological（精神药理学的）、psychopharmacologically（从精神药理学角度）。相关扩展词为 neuropsychopharmacology（神经精神药理学）；基础词族包括 pharmacology（药理学）、pharmacologist（药理学家）、pharmacological（药理学的）和 pharmacologically（从药理学角度）。
morphology_enriched.en: psycho- (mind) + pharmacology → psychopharmacology; a deeper analysis is psycho- + pharmaco- (drug) + -logy (study). The principal direct family comprises psychopharmacologist, psychopharmacologic or psychopharmacological, and psychopharmacologically. A related extended formation is neuropsychopharmacology; the base family includes pharmacology, pharmacologist, pharmacological, and pharmacologically.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 以下是相邻学科或应用名称，并非完全同义词：behavioral pharmacology（行为药理学）更侧重可观察的行为效应；neuropsychopharmacology（神经精神药理学）更突出神经系统机制；psychopharmacotherapy（精神药物治疗）指药物治疗的应用，而非整个研究学科。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: These are overlapping fields or applications rather than exact synonyms: behavioral pharmacology emphasizes observable behavioral effects; neuropsychopharmacology gives particular attention to nervous-system mechanisms; psychopharmacotherapy concerns treatment with psychiatric drugs rather than the entire research discipline.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 心理 psycho- ＋ 药物 pharmaco- ＋ 研究 -logy：研究药物怎样影响心智。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Mind + drugs + study: investigate how medicines and other drugs change mental life.

etymology_story.zh: 表示嘲弄的 razz 是美式口语词，源于 raspberry 的截短或变体；raspberry 在这里指用嘴发出的嘲弄声，而不是水果。这个表示声音的词也发展为动词，意为嘲笑或打趣；扑克名称的来源不宜直接按同一路径断定。
etymology_story.en: In its mocking sense, razz is an American colloquial shortening or alteration of raspberry, meaning a rude sound made with the mouth rather than the fruit. The sound word also became a verb meaning to ridicule or tease; the poker name should not automatically be assigned the same history.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 razz 是不可再作实用拆分的词基。词形与派生：razzes（动词第三人称单数或普通名词复数）、razzed（过去式及过去分词）、razzing（现在分词，也可作名词表示取笑）、razzer（取笑他人的人，较少见）；扑克名称通常作不可数名词。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, razz is a base with no useful internal morphological division. Forms and derivatives include razzes, razzed, razzing, and the less common agent noun razzer; razzing can also function as a noun meaning teasing. The poker name is normally uncountable.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tease（逗弄）通常较轻，也可带亲昵意味；mock（嘲笑）更强调使人显得可笑；taunt（奚落、挑衅）通常更有敌意，意在激怒或伤害对方。razz 属非正式用语，常指朋友间打趣，也可指公开起哄；扑克义没有常用的单词同义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tease is often mild or affectionate; mock emphasizes making someone seem ridiculous; taunt is usually more hostile and intended to provoke or hurt. Razz is informal and often describes friendly teasing, though it can also mean public ridicule. The poker sense has no common single-word synonym.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: raspberry 的嘲弄声缩成 razz：先发怪声，再拿人打趣；扑克义另记“争最低”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A mocking raspberry becomes a razz: first the rude noise, then the teasing. Remember the poker sense separately as aiming low.

etymology_story.zh: rotavirus 是20世纪70年代形成的科学名称，由拉丁语 rota（轮子）和 virus（病毒）组合而成。名称来自病毒颗粒在电子显微镜下呈现的轮状外观。
etymology_story.en: Rotavirus is a scientific name formed in the 1970s from Latin rota, meaning wheel, and virus. It refers to the wheel-like appearance of the virus particles under an electron microscope.

morphology_enriched.zh: rota-（轮，源自拉丁语的构词成分）+ virus（病毒）→ rotavirus。词形与派生：rotaviruses（复数）、rotaviral（轮状病毒的）；rotavirus infection 和 rotavirus vaccine 是以名词作定语的词组，不代表新增形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: Rota-, a Latin-derived element meaning wheel, + virus → rotavirus. Forms and derivatives include rotaviruses and rotaviral. In rotavirus infection and rotavirus vaccine, rotavirus is a noun used attributively, not a separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 没有常用的严格同义词。RV 可在上下文明确时用作缩写；enteric virus（肠道病毒）是更宽泛的描述；norovirus（诺如病毒）是另一类病毒，不能互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no common exact synonym. RV can serve as an abbreviation when the context is clear; enteric virus is a broader description; norovirus names a different group of viruses and is not interchangeable.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: rota 是“轮”：显微镜下像车轮的病毒，就是轮状病毒。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Rota means wheel: picture a wheel-shaped virus under the microscope.

etymology_story.zh: terrarium 是19世纪仿照 aquarium（水族箱）构成的词，以拉丁语 terra（土地）替换与水有关的构词部分。它指把一小片陆地环境置于容器中，用来培育植物或饲养陆生小动物。
etymology_story.en: Terrarium was formed in the nineteenth century on the model of aquarium, using Latin terra, meaning land, in place of the water-related element. It names a container holding a small terrestrial environment for plants or small land animals.

morphology_enriched.zh: terr-（来自 terra，土地）+ -arium（容器、场所）→ terrarium。复数为 terrariums 或 terraria；较少见的形容词为 terrarial（生态箱的）。terrestrial（陆地的）与 terraforming（地球化改造）是同源相关词，并非由 terrarium 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Terr-, from terra meaning land, + -arium, meaning a container or place, → terrarium. The plurals are terrariums and terraria; terrarial is a less common adjective. Terrestrial and terraforming are related through terra, rather than direct derivatives of terrarium.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: vivarium（生物饲养箱）范围更广，常用于饲养动物；bottle garden（瓶中花园）通常指在瓶中种植植物的特定形式；Wardian case（沃德箱）是历史上用于保护、栽培和运输植物的玻璃箱。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Vivarium is broader and is often used for animal enclosures; bottle garden usually describes a particular plant-growing arrangement inside a bottle; Wardian case is a historical term for a glazed enclosure used to protect, grow, and transport plants.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: terra 是“土地”，-arium 是“容器”：把一小片陆地装进玻璃箱。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Terra is land and -arium is a container: a little piece of land inside glass.
