etymology_story.zh: pronate 出现于19世纪，源自晚期拉丁语 pronare（向前弯、俯身）及其过去分词 pronatus，与拉丁语 pronus（前倾的、俯伏的）同源。英语将“转成俯向姿态”的概念专门用于前臂和足部的旋前动作。[历史来源：词源在线](https://www.etymonline.com/word/pronate)；[现代义项与读音：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pronate)。
etymology_story.en: Pronate entered English in the nineteenth century from Late Latin pronare, “to bend forward,” and its participle pronatus, related to Latin pronus, “leaning forward” or “face downward.” English specialized this turning concept for movements of the forearm and foot. [Historical origin: Etymonline](https://www.etymonline.com/word/pronate); [modern senses and pronunciation: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/pronate).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学习可分析为 pron-（俯向、旋前词基）+ -ate（动词形式），但历史上来自拉丁语形式。屈折：pronates、pronated、pronating；派生：pronation（旋前）、pronator（旋前肌），其中 pronation 可按 pronat- + -ion 识记；扩展词族：overpronate／overpronation（过度旋前）、underpronate／underpronation（旋前不足）。pronated 可作分词形容词，表示“处于旋前位的”。
morphology_enriched.en: For modern learning, analyze pron- as the base associated with downward orientation or pronation, plus verbal -ate, while recognizing the Latin origin. Inflections are pronates, pronated, and pronating. Derivatives include pronation, the movement, and pronator, a muscle producing it; pronation can be remembered as pronat- + -ion. Extensions include overpronate/overpronation and underpronate/underpronation. Pronated also functions as a participial adjective meaning positioned in pronation.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: rotate（旋转）范围最广，不限定方向；turn palm-down（把手掌转向下）是前臂义的通俗释义；roll inward（向内滚动）描述步态中的足部动作，但不能替代前臂义。supinate（旋后）是反义词。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Rotate is broader and does not specify direction. Turn palm-down paraphrases the forearm sense. Roll inward describes the foot movement during gait but does not replace the forearm meaning. Supinate is the opposite.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 联想同源词 prone（俯伏的）：前臂旋前，让手掌“俯下”；足部义另记“向内滚动”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect pronate with its relative prone: turn the palm downward. For the foot sense, remember an inward roll.

meaning: 求积；面积或积分的计算

etymology_story.zh: quadrature 在16世纪借自拉丁语 quadratura（使成方形），与 quadrare（使成方形）有关。等面积作方的意义延伸为求积，而正方形的直角关系也体现在天文学和电子学的90度关系中。[义项、读音与词源来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/quadrature)。
etymology_story.en: Quadrature was borrowed in the sixteenth century from Latin quadratura, associated with quadrare, “to make square.” Equal-area squaring developed into integration, while the square's right angle is reflected in the astronomical and electronic senses. [Senses, pronunciation and origin: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/quadrature).

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中为整体借入的学术名词，可按拉丁来源分析为 quadrat-（方形词干）+ -ure（行为或结果名词后缀）。相关词：quadrate（方形的；使成方形）、quadratic（二次的）；常用复合表达：quadrature rule（求积公式）、quadrature component（正交分量）。quadrature 在这些表达中作名词定语，不必另设常用形容词词性。
morphology_enriched.en: This is a borrowed learned noun, analyzable through its Latin structure as quadrat-, a square-related stem, + -ure, an action or result suffix. Related words include quadrate, square-shaped or to make square, and quadratic, relating to the second degree. Compounds include quadrature rule and quadrature component. These use quadrature attributively as a noun rather than establishing a common separate adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: integration（积分）覆盖更广的积分运算，quadrature 常突出具体求积，尤其数值计算；squaring（化为方形）对应历史几何义，但也可能表示“求平方”；phase quadrature（相位正交）明确限定电子学中的90度相位差。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Integration covers integral operations more broadly, while quadrature often emphasizes practical evaluation, especially numerical evaluation. Squaring matches the historical geometric sense but can also mean raising to the second power. Phase quadrature explicitly identifies the electronic 90-degree phase relationship.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“正方形”：面积引出求积，直角引出天体与信号的90度关系。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor everything to a square: its area suggests integration, and its right angle suggests the two 90-degree relationships.

etymology.text: 17世纪从印地语借入，最终联系梵语的鹿名；把这个南亚来源的名字和林间的大型鹿联系起来。

etymology_story.zh: 表示“水鹿”的 sambar 于17世纪从印地语借入，最终联系梵语鹿名 śambara。表示菜肴的 sambar 则来自泰米尔语，是来源不同的同形词，不能把汤名解释成由鹿名演变而来。[两个词源及义项来源：柯林斯词典](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/sambar)。
etymology_story.en: The deer name sambar entered English from Hindi in the seventeenth century and ultimately connects with Sanskrit śambara, a deer name. The culinary word comes from Tamil and is a separate borrowing, not a development of the animal name. [Both origins and senses: Collins Dictionary](https://www.collinsdictionary.com/dictionary/english/sambar).

morphology_enriched.zh: 两个义项在现代英语中都作为整体借词处理，没有可用的英语词缀拆分。动物义为可数名词，复数可用 sambar 或 sambars，异体包括 sambur、sambhur；菜肴义通常不可数，也拼作 sambhar。复合表达包括 sambar deer（水鹿）和 sambar powder（桑巴尔香料粉）；没有常用的动词或形容词派生形式。
morphology_enriched.en: Both meanings are unanalyzed loanwords in modern English, without an English prefix–root–suffix breakdown. The animal noun is countable, with plurals sambar or sambars and variants including sambur and sambhur. The dish noun is normally uncountable and is also spelled sambhar. Compounds include sambar deer and sambar powder, a spice mixture for the dish. Neither meaning has common derived verb or adjective forms.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: sambur（水鹿）是动物名称的异体，意义相同；deer（鹿）是上位词，不能精确指明水鹿；lentil stew（扁豆炖汤）可概括菜肴义，但不一定具有桑巴尔汤典型的罗望子酸味和南印度调味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Sambur is an alternative spelling of the animal name. Deer is a broader category and does not identify the species. Lentil stew describes the food broadly but need not have sambar's characteristic tamarind sourness or South Indian seasoning.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 同形分两格：森林里的大型鹿；餐桌上的酸辣豆汤。两个来源分别记。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Keep two separate pictures: a large deer in the forest and a tangy lentil stew on the table. They represent separate borrowings.

senses.meaning_zh: 皂苷；一类可在水中形成肥皂状泡沫的糖苷
senses.meaning_en: A glycoside that produces soap-like foam in water.
senses.english_definition: A saponin is one of a group of compounds, found mainly in plants, that produce soap-like foam when mixed with water and shaken.
senses.collocation_en: saponin content; saponin extract
senses.collocation_zh: 皂苷含量；皂苷提取物
senses.sentence_en: The researchers measured the saponin content of the seeds.
senses.sentence_zh: 研究人员测定了这些种子的皂苷含量。

etymology_story.zh: 该词于19世纪经法语 saponine 进入英语，最终源于拉丁语 sapo，意为“肥皂”。这一名称来自皂苷水溶液经振摇后产生肥皂状泡沫的性质。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English in the nineteenth century through French saponine, ultimately from Latin sapo, meaning 'soap.' Its name refers to the soap-like foam these compounds produce when shaken in water.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代学术构词可分析为 sapon-（与肥皂有关的词基）+ -in（物质名称后缀）。直接形式包括复数 saponins 和复合形容词 saponin-rich（富含皂苷的）；相关术语 sapogenin（皂苷元）指去除糖基后的部分。同源词包括 saponify（使皂化）、saponification（皂化）和 saponaceous（肥皂状的），但它们并非由 saponin 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: The learned formation is sapon- ('soap') + -in, a substance-forming suffix. Direct forms include the plural saponins and the compound adjective saponin-rich; the related term sapogenin names the portion remaining after the sugars are removed. Saponify, saponification, and saponaceous share the soap-related base but are not direct derivatives of saponin.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: soap-forming glycoside（能起皂沫的糖苷）是解释性近义表达；glycoside（糖苷）是范围更大的上位词；surfactant（表面活性剂）强调表面活性这一功能，包含许多并非皂苷的物质。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Soap-forming glycoside is an explanatory near-equivalent. Glycoside is a broader chemical category, while surfactant describes a function and includes many substances that are not saponins.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: sapon- 联想 soap（肥皂）：摇水起皂沫，想到皂苷。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Link sapon- with soap: shake it in water, see foam, remember saponin.

etymology_story.zh: silvicultural 由 silviculture（森林培育；营林）加形容词后缀 -al 构成。silviculture 中的 silvi- 源于拉丁语 silva（森林），后半部分与表示“耕作、培育”的拉丁语 cultura 有关。
etymology_story.en: Silvicultural was formed from silviculture by adding the adjective suffix -al. Silviculture combines a form of Latin silva, meaning 'forest,' with an element ultimately derived from cultura, meaning 'cultivation.'

morphology_enriched.zh: silvicultur(e) + -al → silvicultural：去掉 silviculture 末尾不发音的 e，再加 -al。主要词族包括 silviculture（营林）、silviculturist／silviculturalist（营林学家；营林工作者）和 silviculturally（在营林方面）。
morphology_enriched.en: Silvicultur(e) + -al → silvicultural: remove the final silent e of silviculture before adding -al. The main word family includes silviculture, silviculturist or silviculturalist, and the adverb silviculturally.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: forestry-related（林业相关的）范围更广，也可涉及林业经济和政策；forest-management（森林经营方面的）与本词接近，但可涵盖更广的经营目标；arboricultural（树木栽培的）通常侧重单株树木，尤其是园林和城市树木。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Forestry-related is broader and can include economics and policy. Forest-management is close but can cover wider management objectives. Arboricultural usually concerns individual trees, especially those in gardens and urban settings.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: silvi- 是“森林”，culture 是“培育”：培育森林，就是营林。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Silvi- means forest and culture suggests cultivation: cultivating a forest is silviculture.

senses.meaning_zh: 美味的；可口的
senses.meaning_en: Delicious or appetizing.

senses.meaning_en: Attractive or desirable, sometimes sexually attractive.

etymology_story.zh: toothsome 于16世纪由 tooth（牙齿）与 -some 构成，最初表达“合口味、可口”的意思。它后来也用于形容令人愉悦或向往的事物，并可在较旧式的用法中表示人的外貌迷人。
etymology_story.en: Toothsome was formed in the sixteenth century from tooth and -some, with the sense 'pleasing to the taste.' It also developed the broader meaning 'attractive or desirable,' including an older use for physical attractiveness.

morphology_enriched.zh: tooth + -some（表示具有某种性质或能引起某种感受）→ toothsome。直接派生词包括 toothsomely（可口地；诱人地）和 toothsomeness（美味；吸引力）；基础词 tooth 的复数为 teeth，相关词有 toothed（有齿的）、toothless（无齿的）和 toothy（露齿的）。
morphology_enriched.en: Tooth + -some, a suffix forming adjectives of characteristic or effect, gives toothsome. Direct derivatives are toothsomely and toothsomeness. The base noun tooth has the plural teeth; related formations include toothed, toothless, and toothy.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: tasty（好吃的）最日常直接；delectable（美味的；令人愉悦的）语气更热情，也可用于比喻；appetizing（令人有食欲的）强调食物看起来或闻起来让人想吃，而 toothsome 通常直接赞美其美味，也带文学色彩。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Tasty is the everyday choice. Delectable expresses stronger delight and can also be figurative. Appetizing emphasizes food's ability to stimulate appetite through its appearance or smell, while toothsome usually praises its deliciousness and sounds literary.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 让牙齿 tooth 忍不住想动起来：可口；再引申为诱人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Something that tempts your teeth is toothsome: delicious first, attractive by extension.

etymology_story.zh: toxoid 于19世纪末由 toxin（毒素）的词干部分与 -oid（类似……的）构成。toxin 最终与希腊语中表示“箭毒”的词有关，而 -oid 源于表示“形状、形式”的希腊语词；名称体现了其保留毒素部分特征但已失去毒性的性质。
etymology_story.en: Toxoid was formed in the late nineteenth century from the stem of toxin and -oid, meaning 'resembling.' Toxin ultimately relates to a Greek word for arrow poison, while -oid derives from a word for form; the name reflects a substance that retains certain properties of a toxin after its toxicity has been removed.

morphology_enriched.zh: tox-（取自 toxin 的词干）+ -oid（类似物）→ toxoid；复数为 toxoids，常见组合有 toxoid vaccine（类毒素疫苗）。相关词族包括 toxin（毒素）、toxic（有毒的）、toxicity（毒性）、toxicology（毒理学）、toxicologist（毒理学家）、detoxify（使解毒）和 detoxification（解毒），这些词并非都由 toxoid 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: Tox-, the stem taken from toxin, + -oid ('a resembling form') gives toxoid; its plural is toxoids, and a common combination is toxoid vaccine. Related vocabulary includes toxin, toxic, toxicity, toxicology, toxicologist, detoxify, and detoxification; these are not all direct derivatives of toxoid.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inactivated toxin（灭活毒素）强调经过失活处理；detoxified toxin（脱毒毒素）强调毒性已被去除；toxoid vaccine（类毒素疫苗）指以类毒素为成分的疫苗制剂，不能在所有语境中与类毒素这一物质本身互换。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Inactivated toxin emphasizes the treatment process, while detoxified toxin emphasizes removal of toxicity. Toxoid vaccine names a vaccine preparation containing a toxoid and is not interchangeable with the substance itself in every context.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tox- 是“毒”，-oid 是“类似”：保留识别特征，去掉毒性。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tox- points to poison; -oid means resembling: keep the recognizable features, remove the toxicity.

etymology_story.zh: Tridentine 源于拉丁语 Tridentinus，意为“特伦托的”，其地名基础是 Tridentum，即今意大利城市特伦托。由于特伦托大公会议于1545至1563年间分期在此举行，该词获得了与会议教义、改革及相关礼仪传统相联系的宗教含义。
etymology_story.en: Tridentine comes from Latin Tridentinus, meaning 'of Trent,' from Tridentum, the Latin name of the Italian city of Trent. Because the Council of Trent met there in sessions between 1545 and 1563, the word acquired its religious associations with the council's doctrines, reforms, and related liturgical traditions.

morphology_enriched.zh: 在现代英语中可识别为 Trident-（拉丁地名 Tridentum 的词干）+ -ine（表示“与……有关的”），但整个词是借入后沿用的形式。名词复数为 Tridentines；相关形式包括 Tridentinism（特伦托会议教义体系）、pre-Tridentine（特伦托会议前的）和 post-Tridentine（特伦托会议后的）。现代词义应从地名理解，不应直接按英语 trident（三叉戟）解释。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English allows the analysis Trident-, the stem of the Latin place name Tridentum, + -ine ('relating to'), although the word was borrowed as an established formation. The noun plural is Tridentines; related forms include Tridentinism, pre-Tridentine, and post-Tridentine. Its modern meaning is tied to the place name rather than directly to the English noun trident.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: Trent-related（与特伦托会议有关的）是会议义的解释性近义表达；traditionalist（传统主义的；传统主义者）范围更广，未必特指该会议；post-Tridentine（特伦托会议后的）首先表示时间关系，不能自动等同于“符合会议教义的”。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Trent-related is an explanatory equivalent for the council-related sense. Traditionalist is broader and need not refer specifically to Trent. Post-Tridentine primarily marks a period after the council and does not automatically mean conformity to its doctrines.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: Tridentum 就是特伦托：记住“城市 → 会议 → 教义与礼仪”。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tridentum is Trent: connect the city to its council, then to its doctrines and liturgy.

etymology_story.zh: 该词形成于现代遗传学术语体系，由表示“三”的 tri- 与表示染色体组倍数的 -ploid 构成，沿用 haploid、diploid 等词的构词模式。这些成分最终与希腊语表示数字和“倍、重”的词形有关。
etymology_story.en: The word developed within modern genetic terminology from tri-, meaning 'three,' and -ploid, indicating the number of chromosome sets, following the pattern of haploid and diploid. These elements ultimately draw on Greek forms expressing numbers and folding or multiplication.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：tri-（三）+ -ploid（具有若干套染色体组的）→ triploid；不要按普通的 -oid（像……的）理解。词族：triploids（三倍体，复数）、triploidy（三倍性）、triploidization（三倍体化）；haploid（单倍体）、diploid（二倍体）、polyploid（多倍体）属于同一构词系列。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: tri- ('three') + -ploid ('having a specified number of chromosome sets') → triploid; the ending should not be interpreted simply as the ordinary suffix -oid, 'resembling.' Family: triploids, triploidy, and triploidization; haploid, diploid, and polyploid belong to the same formation series.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: 无严格的单词近义词：having three chromosome sets（具有三套染色体组）是准确释义；polyploid（多倍体的）范围更广，包括三倍体及更高倍数；三套必须是完整的染色体组，不能理解为仅有三条染色体。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: There is no exact everyday single-word synonym: having three chromosome sets is an accurate paraphrase; polyploid is broader and includes triploids and higher ploidy levels. The three sets must be complete chromosome sets, not merely three individual chromosomes.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: tri-＝三，-ploid＝染色体组套数：三整套，就是三倍体。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Tri- means three; -ploid counts chromosome sets: three complete sets make a triploid.

senses.meaning_zh: 道德败坏；卑劣；卑劣行径

etymology_story.zh: 该词经法语或直接借自拉丁语 turpitudo，后者来自 turpis，意为“丑陋的、可耻的”。拉丁语词本身已兼有外貌丑陋与品行可耻的含义，英语主要保留了道德层面的强烈贬义。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through French or directly from Latin turpitudo, derived from turpis, meaning 'ugly' or 'shameful.' The Latin word already covered both physical ugliness and moral disgrace; English chiefly retained the strongly condemnatory moral meaning.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中通常把 turpitude 作为整体词基记忆，不宜强行拆成可自由组合的现代词缀。历史上，拉丁语 turpis 加抽象名词后缀 -tudo 构成 turpitudo；派生词使用扩展词干 turpitudin-：turpitudinous（道德败坏的，罕用）、turpitudinously（卑劣地，罕用）。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, turpitude is normally treated as a whole lexical base rather than freely assembled from productive affixes. Historically, Latin turpis combined with the abstract-noun suffix -tudo to form turpitudo; derivatives use the extended stem turpitudin-: turpitudinous and turpitudinously, both rare.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: depravity（堕落、邪恶）突出严重的道德腐化；baseness（卑鄙）强调品格低下、行事可耻；wickedness（邪恶）较通用，可强调恶意或恶行。turpitude 更正式，带有强烈的道德谴责意味。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Depravity emphasizes profound moral corruption; baseness stresses dishonorable character and conduct; wickedness is more general and can emphasize malicious intentions or acts. Turpitude is more formal and carries strong moral condemnation.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 把历史词义“丑陋”转向品行：品行之丑，就是 turpitude。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Move the historical idea of ugliness into character: moral ugliness is turpitude.

senses.meaning_zh: 沉沉睡去；因疲倦而迅速入睡，通常与 out 连用
senses.meaning_en: To fall deeply asleep, especially because of exhaustion, usually with out.
senses.english_definition: If you zonk out, you fall deeply asleep, often because you are very tired.
senses.collocation_en: zonk out; zonk out on the sofa
senses.collocation_zh: 沉沉睡去；在沙发上倒头睡着
senses.sentence_en: I zonked out on the sofa as soon as I got home.
senses.sentence_zh: 我一到家就在沙发上倒头睡着了。

senses.meaning_zh: 使昏沉；使失去知觉；使筋疲力尽，常与 out 连用
senses.meaning_en: To make someone dazed, unconscious, or extremely tired, often with out.
senses.english_definition: If something zonks you or zonks you out, it makes you extremely tired, dazed, or unconscious.
senses.collocation_en: zonk someone out; completely zonked
senses.collocation_zh: 使某人昏沉或昏睡；累得精疲力竭
senses.sentence_en: The long journey completely zonked me out.
senses.sentence_zh: 这趟漫长的旅程把我累得昏昏欲睡。

senses.meaning_zh: 猛击；重击，属俚语
senses.meaning_en: To hit or strike someone or something hard, in slang usage.
senses.english_definition: If someone or something zonks a person, they hit that person hard.
senses.collocation_en: zonk someone on the head
senses.collocation_zh: 重击某人的头部
senses.sentence_en: The ball bounced back and zonked him on the head.
senses.sentence_zh: 球弹了回来，重重地砸中了他的头。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是20世纪出现的英语俚语，通常被认为具有拟声性质，使人联想到突然重击的声音。其意义从“重击”扩展到“使昏沉或失去知觉”，而 zonk out 又表示倒头熟睡。
etymology_story.en: This twentieth-century English slang word is generally considered imitative, suggesting the sound of a sudden heavy impact. Its meanings extended from hitting to making someone dazed or unconscious, while zonk out developed the sense of falling deeply asleep.

morphology_enriched.zh: zonk 是不可再作实用拆分的词基。屈折形式：zonks、zonked、zonking；zonked 也常独立用作形容词，表示“精疲力竭的、昏沉的”；zonk out 是常用短语动词，zonked-out 是相应的复合形容词。
morphology_enriched.en: Zonk is a lexical base with no useful internal morphological division. Inflected forms: zonks, zonked, and zonking; zonked also commonly functions as an adjective meaning 'exhausted' or 'dazed.' Zonk out is a common phrasal verb, and zonked-out is its corresponding compound adjective.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: crash out（倒头就睡）同样口语化，突出疲倦后迅速入睡；doze off（打起盹来）通常指较轻、较短的睡眠；knock out（使昏迷、使失去知觉）突出外力造成的意识丧失。zonk out 往往带有累得一下睡沉的生动语气。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Crash out is similarly informal and emphasizes falling asleep quickly from tiredness; doze off usually suggests lighter or shorter sleep; knock out emphasizes unconsciousness caused by an external force. Zonk out often vividly suggests suddenly falling into a deep, exhausted sleep.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 想象“咚”地倒下：被击得昏沉，或累得倒头睡着。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Picture a sudden thud: someone is struck senseless or drops straight into exhausted sleep.

meaning: 闭锁；身体管道缺如或不通

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

forms: 可数或不可数；复数 atresias 用于不同种类或病例。
family: atretic 闭锁的

morphology.text: a- + tres- + -ia → atresia（无正常开口的状态）；a- 表示无，tres- 联系穿孔，-ia 表示状态。

etymology.text: 19世纪通过新拉丁语进入英语，来自希腊语 atretos（未穿孔的）；想成原本应有的通道没有正常开口。

usage_note: 医学名词，常由部位名限定，如 biliary atresia；本课解释术语，不涉及治疗判断。

answers: 闭锁；身体管道缺如或不通

senses.meaning_zh: 闭锁；正常身体开口或管道的缺如或封闭
senses.meaning_en: The absence or closure of a normal bodily opening or passage.
senses.english_definition: Atresia is a condition in which a normal opening or passage in the body is missing or closed.
senses.collocation_en: biliary atresia; esophageal atresia
senses.collocation_zh: 胆道闭锁；食管闭锁
senses.sentence_en: The infant was diagnosed with esophageal atresia shortly after birth.
senses.sentence_zh: 这名婴儿出生后不久便被诊断为食管闭锁。

senses.meaning_zh: 卵泡闭锁；未排卵卵泡的退化与吸收
senses.meaning_en: The degeneration and resorption of ovarian follicles that do not ovulate.
senses.english_definition: In reproductive biology, atresia is the process in which an ovarian follicle degenerates and is absorbed instead of releasing an egg.
senses.collocation_en: follicular atresia; undergo atresia
senses.collocation_zh: 卵泡闭锁；发生闭锁退化
senses.sentence_en: Most ovarian follicles undergo atresia rather than ovulation.
senses.sentence_zh: 大多数卵泡会发生闭锁退化，而不会排卵。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经新拉丁语医学用语进入英语，追溯至希腊语 atrētos，意为“未穿孔的”，其中 a- 表示“无”，trētos 表示“穿通的”。其核心意义是缺少正常开口，后来也用于命名卵泡退化的过程。
etymology_story.en: The word entered English through medical New Latin and goes back to Greek atrētos, meaning 'unperforated,' with a- meaning 'without' and trētos meaning 'perforated.' Its central meaning concerns the absence of a normal opening, and the term also came to name the degeneration of ovarian follicles.

morphology_enriched.zh: 一般英语中将 atresia 作为整体医学术语记忆；词源分析可概括为希腊语 a-（无）+ trēt-（穿通）+ 名词性词尾，不能把 tres 当作独立的现代英语词根。核心词族：atresia（闭锁）、atretic（闭锁的；发生卵泡闭锁的，使用 atret- 词干）；复数为 atresias。
morphology_enriched.en: In general English, atresia is treated as a whole medical term; its historical structure can be summarized as Greek a- ('without') + trēt- ('perforated') + a nominal ending, rather than treating tres as an independent modern English root. Core family: atresia and atretic, which uses the stem atret-; the plural is atresias.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: occlusion（闭塞）泛指开口或通道被关闭；obstruction（梗阻）突出存在阻碍通行的因素；stenosis（狭窄）指通道变窄，并不必然完全不通。这些词都不能普遍替代 atresia，尤其不能直接替代其“卵泡退化”义。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Occlusion broadly means closure of an opening or passage; obstruction emphasizes something blocking passage; stenosis means narrowing and does not necessarily imply complete closure. None is a universal substitute for atresia, particularly in its sense of follicular degeneration.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: a-＝无，历史词根＝穿通：本该通的地方没有通。
mnemonic_anchor.en: A- means without, and the historical base means perforated: a passage that should be open is not.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

forms: 形容词无复数或时态；比较程度可用 more/most biomorphic。
family: biomorph 生物形态图形；biomorphic design 生物形态设计

morphology.text: bio- + morph + -ic → biomorphic（具有生物形态的）；bio- 指生命，morph 指形态。

etymology.text: 英语用源于希腊语的 bios（生命）与 morphe（形态）等构词成分组成；看到像叶片、细胞或身体的轮廓便容易记住。

usage_note: 常用于艺术和设计，形状让人联想到生命体；不表示物品本身活着或由生物材料制成。

senses.meaning_zh: 具有生物形态的；形似生物或有机生命形态的
senses.meaning_en: Resembling the shapes or forms of living organisms.
senses.english_definition: A biomorphic shape or design resembles the form of a living organism, often without representing one exactly.
senses.collocation_en: biomorphic forms; biomorphic abstraction
senses.collocation_zh: 生物形态；生物形态抽象艺术
senses.sentence_en: The sculpture's biomorphic curves suggest leaves and growing cells.
senses.sentence_zh: 这座雕塑具有生物形态的曲线，让人联想到叶片和生长中的细胞。

etymology_story.zh: 该词由源自希腊语 bios（生命）和 morphē（形态）的英语构词成分组合而成。它尤其用于艺术与设计，描述使人联想到生物、有机体或生命生长的形态。
etymology_story.en: The word was formed in English from combining elements derived from Greek bios, 'life,' and morphē, 'form.' It is used especially in art and design for shapes that evoke organisms, organic structures, or living growth.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代构词：bio-（生命、生物）+ morph（形态）+ -ic（……的）→ biomorphic。核心词族：biomorph（生物形态的图形或物体）、biomorphism（生物形态主义；生物形态表现）、biomorphically（以生物形态方式，较少见）。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern formation: bio- ('life or living organisms') + morph ('form') + -ic ('relating to') → biomorphic. Core family: biomorph, a figure or object with an organic form; biomorphism, the use or representation of such forms; and biomorphically, a less common adverb.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: organic（有机的、自然生长般的）范围更宽，可强调自然感或整体性；zoomorphic（兽形的）专指动物形态；biomimetic（仿生的）通常强调模仿生物的结构、过程或功能。biomorphic 主要描述外形与生物形态相似。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Organic is broader and may emphasize natural growth or an integrated whole; zoomorphic specifically means animal-shaped; biomimetic usually emphasizes imitation of biological structures, processes, or functions. Biomorphic chiefly describes visual resemblance to living forms.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: bio＝生命，morph＝形态：把生命的轮廓变成设计。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Bio means life and morph means form: living shapes become design.

meaning: 慕道者；受洗前接受教理指导者

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

forms: 可数名词；复数 catechumens。
family: catechumenal 慕道者的；catechumenate 慕道期

morphology.text: catechumen + -al → catechumenal（慕道者的）；catechumen 整词作为独立词素记忆。

etymology.text: 经晚期拉丁语 catechumenus 联系希腊语 katechoumenos，意思是正在接受口头教导的人；把它记成受洗前学习教理的人。

usage_note: 基督教术语，本课教受洗前接受指导的人；不要和负责施教的 catechist 混淆。

translation: 这位慕道者在受洗前每周参加教理课程。

instruct a catechumen before baptism 在受洗前指导慕道者

senses.meaning_zh: 慕道者；受洗前接受基督教教理指导的人
senses.meaning_en: a person receiving instruction in Christianity before baptism
senses.english_definition: A catechumen is someone who is learning about the Christian faith in preparation for baptism.
senses.collocation_en: instruct catechumens; prepare catechumens for baptism
senses.collocation_zh: 向慕道者传授教理；帮助慕道者准备受洗
senses.sentence_en: The catechumens met each week to study the Christian faith before their baptism.
senses.sentence_zh: 这些慕道者在受洗前每周聚会，学习基督教信仰。

etymology_story.zh: 该词经教会拉丁语 catechumenus 源自希腊语 katēkhoumenos，意为“正在接受口头教导的人”，与表示“使声音回响；口头教导”的 katēkhein 有关。在早期基督教中，它成为对接受教理指导、准备受洗者的专称。
etymology_story.en: The word came through ecclesiastical Latin catechumenus from Greek katēkhoumenos, meaning 'a person being instructed orally,' from katēkhein, 'to sound into the ears; instruct orally.' In early Christianity, it became a specific term for someone receiving religious instruction before baptism.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语中 catechumen 通常作为完整借词处理，不宜硬拆成常用英语词缀。词族：catechumens（复数）；catechumen + -al → catechumenal（慕道者的；慕道培育的）；catechumen + -ical → catechumenical（慕道者的，较少见）；catechumen + -ate → catechumenate（慕道阶段、制度或慕道者群体）。历史同源词包括 catechesis（教理讲授）、catechist（教理讲授者）和 catechize（讲授教理；通过问答教导），它们并非由 catechumen 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: In modern English, catechumen is normally treated as a complete borrowed base rather than divided into productive English affixes. Its family includes catechumens, the plural; catechumen + -al → catechumenal, relating to catechumens or their formation; catechumen + -ical → catechumenical, a less common adjective; and catechumen + -ate → catechumenate, the period, system, or body of catechumens. Historical relatives include catechesis, religious instruction; catechist, a religious instructor; and catechize, to teach religious principles or instruct through questions and answers. These are not direct derivatives of catechumen.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: inquirer（信仰探询者）通常仍在了解信仰，未必正式进入慕道阶段；candidate for baptism（受洗候选人）强调准备接受洗礼，具体身份依教会传统而异；novice（初学者；初修者）的范围更广，在修会语境中通常指接受入会训练的人。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: An inquirer is exploring a faith and may not yet have entered formal preparation; a candidate for baptism is identified by the intended sacrament, with the precise status varying by church tradition; a novice is a beginner more generally and, in a religious order, usually someone undergoing initial training.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: 抓住“口头教导”的历史核心：先听教理，再准备受洗。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Anchor it to oral instruction: hearing the teaching before receiving baptism.

pronunciation.note: 采用英式音标。

forms: 可数名词；复数 centimes。
family: centim 生丁的相关拼写；cent 百分之一货币单位

morphology.text: cent- + -ime → centime（百分之一的货币单位），这是借入词中的法语构词线索。

etymology.text: 18世纪从法语借入，联系古法语 centiesme 和拉丁语 centesimus（第一百）；把一法郎分成一百份来记。

usage_note: 本课按法郎的百分之一理解；阅读旧法国资料时要注意历史货币背景，也见于其他使用法郎的地区。

etymology_story.zh: 该词借自法语 centime，其历史来源是拉丁语 centesimus，意为“第一百；百分之一”。它在法国采用十进制货币制度的背景下成为货币单位名称，后来也用于其他法语货币语境。
etymology_story.en: The word was borrowed from French centime and ultimately comes from Latin centesimus, meaning 'hundredth.' It became a monetary term with the adoption of decimal currency in France and was subsequently used in other French-language currency contexts.

morphology_enriched.zh: 现代英语将 centime 作为完整借入的名词，规则复数为 centimes。cent- 可作为“百”的历史词根线索，但不应把 -ime 当作能自由造词的英语后缀；cent（分）、centesimal（百分的；百分制的）属于相关词根网络，并非 centime 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Modern English treats centime as a complete borrowed noun, with the regular plural centimes. The element cent- provides a historical clue meaning 'hundred,' but -ime is not a productive English suffix. Cent, a hundredth-unit coin, and centesimal, relating to hundredths or division into a hundred parts, belong to the related root network rather than being direct derivatives of centime.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: cent（分）也是某些货币的百分之一单位，但名称随币种而定，不能随意替换 centime；penny（便士）通常指英镑的百分之一单位，也可在北美口语中指一美分硬币；small change（零钱）泛指小面额钱币，不表示固定币值。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A cent is also a hundredth-unit denomination, but its name depends on the currency and is not freely interchangeable with centime; a penny usually means a hundredth of a pound, or informally a one-cent coin in North America; small change means low-denomination money collectively, without specifying a fixed value.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: cent- 联想“一百”：一法郎分成一百份，每份一生丁。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Connect cent- with one hundred: divide a franc into one hundred parts, and each part is a centime.

senses.meaning_en: a person who loves chocolate and eats it very enthusiastically
senses.english_definition: If you call someone a chocoholic, you mean humorously that they love chocolate and find it difficult to resist eating it.
senses.collocation_en: a self-confessed chocoholic; a chocoholic's dream
senses.collocation_zh: 一个自认的巧克力迷；巧克力迷梦寐以求的东西

senses.sentence_zh: 她自认是个巧克力迷，总是点巧克力甜点。

etymology_story.zh: 该词是二十世纪英语中的幽默造词，由 chocolate 的缩略部分与仿照 alcoholic 形成的 -holic 结合而成。它把“难以抗拒某物”的说法用于巧克力，通常表示强烈喜爱，并不自动表示医学意义上的成瘾。
etymology_story.en: This humorous twentieth-century formation combines a shortened form of chocolate with -holic, modeled on alcoholic. It applies the idea of finding something irresistible to chocolate and normally expresses strong enthusiasm rather than a medical diagnosis of addiction.

morphology_enriched.zh: choco(late) + -holic → chocoholic；-holic 是从 alcoholic 重新分析出来、表示“对某事物特别着迷的人”的构词成分，并非独立的古典词根。词族：chocoholics（复数）、chocoholism（对巧克力的强烈迷恋，幽默用法）；变体拼写为 chocaholic，相应名词也可写作 chocaholism。基础词 chocolate 的相关形式有 chocolates（巧克力糖；复数形式）和 chocolatey／chocolaty（有巧克力味或质感的）。
morphology_enriched.en: choco(late) + -holic → chocoholic. The formative -holic was reanalyzed from alcoholic to mean someone strongly attached to an activity or substance; it is not an independent classical root. The family includes chocoholics, the plural, and chocoholism, a humorous term for an intense attachment to chocolate. Variant spellings include chocaholic and chocaholism. Forms associated with the base chocolate include chocolates, individual chocolate sweets or the plural form, and chocolatey/chocolaty, having the taste or texture of chocolate.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: chocolate lover（巧克力爱好者）语气中性，只强调喜爱；chocolate addict（巧克力上瘾者）更突出难以克制，日常也常是夸张说法；sweet tooth（爱吃甜食的嗜好）涵盖各种甜食，通常用于 have a sweet tooth，不能直接当作人的同义称呼。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A chocolate lover is a neutral term emphasizing enjoyment; a chocolate addict more strongly suggests difficulty resisting chocolate, though it is often hyperbolic in everyday speech; a sweet tooth is a liking for sweet foods generally, normally used in have a sweet tooth, rather than a direct name for a person.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: choco 是巧克力，-holic 是“迷”：看到巧克力就难以抗拒的人。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Choco supplies the chocolate; -holic supplies the irresistible enthusiasm.

etymology_story.zh: 该词源于希腊语 khthōn（土地；大地）及相关形容词 khthonios（大地的；地下的），在十九世纪进入英语。它在古典宗教研究中主要描述与大地、亡者和冥界有关的神灵或力量。
etymology_story.en: The word derives from Greek khthōn, 'earth' or 'ground,' and the related adjective khthonios, 'of the earth; beneath the earth,' and entered English in the nineteenth century. In the study of ancient religion, it chiefly describes deities or powers associated with the earth, the dead, and the underworld.

morphology_enriched.zh: chthon-（大地；地下）+ -ic（……的）→ chthonic。相关形式包括 chthonian（地下的；冥界的，近义形容词）和 chthonically（以地下或冥界相关的方式，罕见副词）。同根词 autochthon（原住民；本地起源者）与 autochthonous（土生土长的；本地起源的）含 auto-（自身）与同一个“大地”词根，但不是由 chthonic 直接派生。
morphology_enriched.en: chthon-, 'earth' or 'beneath the earth,' + -ic, 'relating to,' → chthonic. Related forms include chthonian, an adjective with a similar meaning, and chthonically, a rare adverb meaning in a manner associated with the earth or underworld. The cognates autochthon, an original inhabitant or locally originating being, and autochthonous, indigenous or locally originating, combine auto-, 'self,' with the same earth root; they are not direct derivatives of chthonic.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: underworld（冥界的，作名词定语时）是较直白的神话语境表达；subterranean（地下的）侧重实际空间位置，不必涉及宗教；infernal（地狱的）更容易带有地狱、恶魔或邪恶的意味，而 chthonic 本身不必表示邪恶。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: Underworld, used attributively, is a plainer mythological alternative; subterranean emphasizes physical location below ground without necessarily implying religion; infernal more readily suggests hell, demons, or evil, whereas chthonic does not inherently mean evil.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: chthon-＝大地：把视线从天空移到地下，就到了冥界神灵的领域。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Chthon- means earth: look beneath the ground to reach the realm of underworld deities.

etymology_story.zh: 该词来自拉丁语 congener，意为“同类的；同族的”，由表示“共同”的 con- 与表示“种类；族类”的词干 gener- 构成。英语中的一般“同类成员”义后来发展出分类学上的“同属物种”和化学上的相关物质等专门含义。
etymology_story.en: The word comes from Latin congener, meaning 'of the same kind or stock,' formed from con-, 'together,' and gener-, a stem meaning 'kind' or 'stock.' Its general English meaning of a related member developed specialized applications to organisms in the same genus and to associated or structurally related chemical substances.

morphology_enriched.zh: 历史构词为 con-（共同）+ gener-（种类；族类）；现代英语通常将 congener 作为完整名词使用。词族：congeners（复数）；congener 对应形容词 congeneric（同属的；同类的），可理解为 congener 词干加形容词后缀并发生词干变化；congenerous（同类的；同性质的，较少见）。genus（属；种类）与 generic（类的；通用的）是相关同源词，不是 congener 的直接派生词。
morphology_enriched.en: Historically, the word combines con-, 'together,' with gener-, 'kind' or 'stock'; modern English normally uses congener as a complete noun. Its family includes congeners, the plural; congeneric, an adjective meaning of the same genus or kind, formed with an adjective suffix and a stem adjustment; and congenerous, a less common adjective meaning of the same kind or nature. Genus, a taxonomic group or kind, and generic, relating to a class or being general, are historical relatives rather than direct derivatives of congener.

synonyms_and_nuances.zh: relative（近亲；相关事物）只表示存在联系，不保证同属或同一化学系列；counterpart（对应物）强调功能、地位或作用相当；analogue（类似物；结构类似物）强调相似性，化学语境中与 congener 有时重叠，但后者更突出同一相关类别中的成员身份。
synonyms_and_nuances.en: A relative is connected by ancestry or another relationship without necessarily sharing a genus or chemical series; a counterpart corresponds in function, position, or role; an analogue resembles something, often structurally in chemistry, and can overlap with congener, which more specifically emphasizes membership in a related group.

mnemonic_anchor.zh: con-＝共同，gener-＝种类：同一类里的“亲戚”，可以是物种，也可以是化合物。
mnemonic_anchor.en: Con- means together and gener- means kind: a congener is a relative within the same group, whether an organism or a chemical.
